# iRender: full LLM context

Generated by tools/llm-docs.sh. Sections: authoring rules, components, core README, then each kit's README. Icon names are in skills/irender/references/icons.md.


---

# Writing iRender documents

iRender renders UI from a JSON or YAML document. This page is the compact set of rules for writing one that validates on the first try. Component props are in `components.md`; each kit's details are in its own file.

## Document

```yaml
version: 1
lang: es                                                # optional: the page's language
labels: { "Rows per page": "Filas por página" }         # optional: the kits' interface text, by its English
theme: { tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } } }   # optional
state: { count: 0, tab: overview, results: [] }         # optional: browser state, every key you read or set
fragments: { card: { type: stack, children: [] } }      # optional: reusable subtrees
root: { type: stack, children: [] }                     # required: one node
```

Only these seven top-level keys exist. Unknown keys are errors. For a page in another language, set `lang` and give `labels` for the kits' fixed words: [labels.md](labels.md) lists every key, and `{ one, other }` gives a count's plural forms.

## Node

```yaml
type: button                 # required: a component name
props: { label: Save }       # the component's props (see components.md); typed and validated
attrs: { id: save, aria-label: Save }   # any HTML attribute; wins over the component's own
class: [cta]                 # extra class names
style: { padding: 12px 20px, ":hover": { opacity: 0.9 }, "@md": { padding: 16 } }
parts: { label: { style: { font-weight: 600 } } }   # style a component's inner elements (names in components.md)
on: { click: { action: set_state, key: count, value: "{{ count + 1 }}" } }
children: []
```

Only these eight keys exist on a node. Components that say `children: no` take none.

## Built-in components (always available)

`element` (any tag via `props.tag`), `text`, `stack`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `list`, `if`, plus `else` and `include`, which the loader resolves.

| kit | flag | adds |
|---|---|---|
| ui-kit | `--ui-kit` | `ui-*` components in the style of shadcn/ui, and a theme with dark mode and theme options |
| chart-kit | `--chart-kit` | `ui-chart`, `ui-sparkline`, `ui-live-data` (Apache ECharts) |
| flow-kit | `--flow-kit` | `ui-flow` and its `ui-flow-*` templates: node-and-edge diagrams |
| icon-kit | `--icon-kit` | `ui-icon`, and icon names in `icon` props of ui-kit components |

Prefer ui-kit components over hand-styled `element`s whenever a kit is in use. They are accessible, themed and dark-mode aware.

## Expressions

Any string may contain `{{ … }}`.

- **Grammar:** paths (`user.name`, `items[0]`, `row['first-name']`, `cart.length`), string, number, boolean and `null` literals, arithmetic `+ - * / %`, comparisons `== != < <= > >=`, `&& || !`, `a ? b : c` and parentheses.
- **Functions:** only `range(n)` / `range(start, end)`, `includes(list, value)` and `toggle(list, value)`. There are no others: no `map`, `filter`, `join`, `toUpperCase`, `Math.*`, template literals or arrow functions.
- **No array or object literals inside `{{ }}`:** write the structure in YAML or JSON instead, with expressions in its leaves: `value: { title: Saved, description: "Hi {{ name }}", tags: ["{{ tag }}"] }`. An action's object or list is filled in when the action runs.
- **Paths only:** `.field` and `[i]` follow paths, not call results (`range(n).length` is invalid).
- **Live or server-side:** a path whose first name is a `state` key updates live in the browser. Any other path is filled from server `data` at render time. Inside a `list`, `item` and `index` (or the `as` / `index` names) are in scope.
- **Exact values:** a string that is only one expression keeps the value's type (`"{{ count }}"` is a number). Mixed text makes a string: `"Buy {{ qty }}"`.

## State and actions

- **Declare state:** every state key an action sets, a control `bind`s or an expression reads live must be declared in `state` with its starting value. Undeclared keys are errors.
- **Top-level keys only:** `bind` and `set_state` `key` take a top-level key, never a path like `draft.customer`. A form needs one flat key per field (`customer`, `product`), which `submit` then gathers in its `body`.
- **Event names:** `on` maps a DOM event (`click`, `input`, `change`, `submit`, `keydown`, …) or `mount` (when the element first appears) to one action or a list. A list runs in order, and `submit` waits for its response.

| action | fields |
|---|---|
| `set_state` | `key`, `value` (usually an expression) |
| `navigate` | `url` |
| `submit` | `endpoint`, `method` (default POST), `body` (object; a query string for GET), `into` (state key for the JSON response), `invalidates` (records of `ui-data-source`s fetched again once it succeeds: `[people]`, or `{ people: "{{ person.id }}" }`) |
| `call` | `name`, `args`: dispatches an `irender:call` DOM event for the host app |
| `wait` | `ms` (at most 60000) |

There is no other action and no inline JavaScript. Anything custom goes through `call`.

- **What gets evaluated:** in actions, every `{{ }}` is, however deep: a `set_state` value, each field of `submit`'s `body` (`body: { customer: "{{ customer }}" }`) and `call`'s `args`, objects and lists in them included. In component props, the component decides (a column's `{{ row.x }}` is filled per row).
- **`submit` failures:** they don't stop the chain. A non-2xx response is still stored in `into`, and a network error fires an `irender:error` DOM event. Either way, the following actions run. Success fires `irender:submitted` with `{ ok, status, data }`. To act only on success, show the outcome with an `if` on the response stored in `into` (e.g. `{{ saved.id }}`), or let the host handle the request through `call`.
- **Forms:** `on.submit` on an `element` with `tag: form` whose actions include `submit` prevents the browser's own navigation.

## Form controls

`input`, `select` and `textarea`, and their `ui-*` versions, take `bind: <state key>` for two-way binding. A checkbox binds a boolean. A radio needs a `value`. `select` / `ui-select` `options` are values or `{ value, label, disabled }`.

## Conditionals and lists

```yaml
- { type: if, props: { when: "{{ step == 1 }}" }, children: [ … ] }
- { type: else, props: { when: "{{ step == 2 }}" }, children: [ … ] }   # else-if; must directly follow an if/else
- { type: else, children: [ … ] }

- type: list
  props: { items: "{{ results }}", as: r, key: "{{ r.id }}", tag: ul }   # key keeps DOM (inputs, focus) across updates
  children: [ { type: text, props: { tag: li, value: "{{ r.title }}" } } ]
```

- `if` adds no element of its own. `list` wraps its items in a `div` unless you give it a `tag` such as `ul` or `tbody`.
- **Mixed conditions:** an `if` inside a server-rendered list may mix the item and state, as in `"{{ filter == null || row.status == filter }}"`. The item part is filled in per row on the server, and the state part stays live.
- Repeat something n times: `items: "{{ range(n) }}"`.
- Keep a set of choices in state: `includes(tags, 'x')` and `toggle(tags, 'x')`.

## Fragments

```yaml
fragments:
  stat:
    type: stack
    children: [ { type: text, props: { value: "{{ label }}" } }, { type: text, props: { value: "{{ value }}" } } ]
root:
  type: stack
  children:
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: Revenue, value: "{{ totals.revenue }}" } } }
```

`name` must be a fixed string. Use fragments for anything repeated more than twice with different values.

## Styles and theme

- **Properties:** `style` accepts any CSS property, in kebab-case. Numbers get `px` where it makes sense.
- **Tokens:** `$group.name` compiles to `var(--group-name)`, and an unknown token is an error. Default tokens:
  - `color.primary`, `primary-hover`, `on-primary`, `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `border`
  - `radius.sm` / `md` / `lg`
  - `space.xs` / `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`
  - `font.body`, `font.size.sm` / `md` / `lg`
- **ui-kit tokens:** the kit adds `color.secondary`, `accent`, `subtle`, `destructive`, `ring` and others. Add your own under `theme.tokens`.
- **Nested blocks:** `":hover"`, `"&.active"`, `"& > li"`, `"@sm"` / `"@md"` / `"@lg"` / `"@xl"` (min-width breakpoints), `"@dark"`, `"@print"`, `"@motion-safe"`, `"@media (…)"`.
- **Dynamic values:** `color: "{{ ok ? 'green' : 'crimson' }}"` updates live. `null` leaves the property unset.
- **Dark mode:** use tokens, not literal colours, so dark mode works. `theme.modes.dark` overrides tokens.

## YAML pitfalls

- **Expressions:** quote any value that starts with `{{` or `{`, or YAML reads it as a mapping. Write `value: "{{ count }}"`, never `value: {{ count }}`.
- **Hex colours:** quote them (`"#4f46e5"`), or `#` starts a comment.
- **Style keys:** quote any key starting with `:`, `@` or `&`, such as `":hover"`, `"@md"` and `"&.active"`.
- **Flow maps:** they are fine for short nodes (`{ type: text, props: { value: Hi } }`). Use block style once a node has children.

## Workflow

1. **Kits:** decide which ones the page needs, and pass the same flags to every command.
2. **Props:** look up each component's props in `components.md` (or run `irender components --ui-kit …`). Don't guess prop names.
3. **Write:** write the document. Put sample server data in a separate `*.data.json` if it reads any.
4. **Validate:** run `irender validate page.yaml --ui-kit …`. It lists every problem with its path, such as `root.children[1].on.click[0].key: 'n' is not declared in 'state'`. Fix them all and repeat until it passes. Treat warnings (unknown CSS) as worth fixing.
5. **Render:** run `irender render page.yaml --data page.data.json --ui-kit … -o page.html`, then open it in a browser to check it.
6. **Untrusted input:** for documents from users or other models, validate and render with `--untrusted`.

## Common mistakes

- **Undeclared state:** setting or binding a key missing from `state`.
- **Unsupported expressions:** JavaScript-only syntax such as `.map(`, `.toFixed(`, `${}`, `===`, `=>`, or `[…]` and `{…}` literals.
- **Missing kit flag:** a `ui-*` component without `--ui-kit` is "unknown component type".
- **Wrong place for a value:** a prop under `attrs`, or an attribute under `props`. Component props go in `props`, and raw HTML attributes such as `id`, `aria-*` and `href` on an `element` go in `attrs`.
- **Children where none are allowed:** giving children to `text`, `input`, `ui-input`, `ui-badge` or other components marked `children: no`. Use `element` or `stack` to group.
- **Bad `else`:** an `else` that doesn't directly follow an `if`, or one that follows a plain `else` (only `else` with `when` can be followed).
- **Layout by hand:** hand-writing flex layout with `element` instead of `stack` (`direction`, `gap`, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`).
- **Literal colours:** they break dark mode. Use `$color.*`.
- **Toggle groups reset to `null`:** pressing a selected `ui-toggle-group` option again sets its key to `null`, so a filter must treat `null` as "all".
- **Dialogs that stay open:** a submit button inside a `ui-dialog` doesn't close it. Use a `ui-dialog-close` whose `on.click` runs the `submit` (and any toast), so it sends and closes in one click.
- **Missing table components:** `ui-table` has no row or cell components. Its children are `element`s with `tag: thead`, `tbody`, `tr`, `th` and `td`, or a `list` with `tag: tbody`.


---


# Components

Every component with all kits enabled. Each entry: name and summary, then one line per prop (name, type, description), its `parts`, and whether it takes `children`. Core built-ins come first, then `ui-*` (ui-kit), `ui-chart` / `ui-sparkline` / `ui-live-data` (chart-kit), `ui-flow*` (flow-kit), `ui-map*` (map-kit), `ui-twin*` (twin-kit) and `ui-icon` (icon-kit).

```
element: Any HTML element. Set attributes with `attrs`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag name (default `div`)
  children: yes
text: Text content.
  value        any (required)  The text. Templates update live when they use `state`.
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `span`), e.g. `h1`, `p`, `li`
  children: no
stack: Flex layout container.
  direction    one of: row, column, row-reverse, column-reverse  Default `column`
  gap          any  Number (px, following the theme's `space.scale` and `space.gap`), CSS length or `$token`
  align        any  `align-items`
  justify      any  `justify-content`
  wrap         bool  Wrap children onto multiple lines
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`)
  children: yes
button: A button. Wire it up with `on.click`.
  label        any  Button text, rendered in the `label` part
  variant      one of: primary, secondary, ghost  Default `primary`
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: label
  children: yes
input: Form input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the value (`checked` for checkboxes)
  type         string  Input type (default `text`)
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name (bound radios default to the `bind` key)
  value        any  Initial value when not bound; for a bound radio, the value it stands for
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
select: Dropdown.
  options      any (required)  Array of values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. Rebuilt in the browser when it uses state.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the selected value (a list of them with `multiple`)
  multiple     bool  Several can be picked (a list box; Ctrl or ⌘ and a click, Shift for a run); the key holds a list
  placeholder  any  Text of a first, empty option (not with `multiple`)
  name         string  Form field name
  value        any  Initially selected value when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
textarea: Multi-line text input.
  bind         statekey  State key kept in sync with the text
  placeholder  any  
  name         string  Form field name
  rows         any  Visible lines (default 3)
  value        any  Initial text when not bound
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: no
list: Renders its children once per item. Rebuilt in the browser when `items` uses state.
  items        any (required)  An array: `{{ data.path }}`, or `{{ state_key }}` to rebuild in the browser
  as           string  Name of the current item (default `item`)
  index        string  Name of the current index (default `index`)
  tag          tag  HTML tag (default `div`), e.g. `ul`
  key          any  Per-item key, e.g. `{{ item.id }}`. When the browser rebuilds the list, items whose key survives keep their nodes
  children: yes
if: Renders its children when `when` is truthy. Adds no element of its own. A following `else` (with `when` for else-if) renders when it doesn't.
  when         any (required)  Condition. Shown and hidden in the browser when it uses state.
  children: yes
ui-button: A button in six variants and four sizes. With `href` it is a link that looks like a button.
  label        any  Button text
  icon         any  An icon name (with the icon kit) or a character, before the label
  variant      one of: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand  Default `default`
  size         one of: default, sm, lg, icon  Default `default`
  href         any  Render a link that looks like a button
  type         one of: button, submit, reset  Default `button`
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  children: yes
ui-camera: Takes photos: front and back camera, light, zoom, composing lines, a timer, retakes and several shots, made smaller before they're kept. Where there's no camera to use, the device's own picker.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the photo, `{ id, url, name, type, size, width, height, at }` (`url` is a `data:` address), or with `multiple` a list of them
  multiple     bool  Several photos
  max          number  At most this many
  facing       one of: back, front  The camera it starts with (default `back`)
  ratio        any  The photo's shape, e.g. `1` or `"4 / 3"` (default the camera's)
  maxSize      number  The photo's longer side at most, in px (default 1600)
  quality      number  0 to 1 (default 0.8)
  type         one of: jpeg, webp, png  Default `jpeg`
  review       bool  Each photo is looked at first, to use or retake (default true, or false with `multiple`)
  grid         bool  Lines for composing start shown
  timer        number  Seconds between the button and the photo (default 0)
  guide        one of: none, card, face, square  An outline to fill
  stamp        any  Written along the foot of the photo, e.g. `{{ site }} · {{ now }}`; `time` is the date and time
  files        bool  Photos can be chosen from the device too (default true)
  autoStart    bool  The camera starts by itself, where it's been allowed
  label        any  The button that starts it (default `Open the camera`)
  disabled     any  Shown, not changed
  children: no
ui-permission-manager: What the app may use (camera, location, notifications…): why, whether it's allowed, a button to ask, and how to allow what was blocked.
  permissions  any (required)  What's used: names, or `{ name, label, reason, required }`: `camera`, `microphone`, `geolocation`, `notifications`, `motion`, `storage` (kept when space is short), `clipboard` or `nfc`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets each one's answer, e.g. `{ camera: granted, geolocation: prompt }`: `granted`, `denied`, `prompt` or `unsupported`
  bindReady    statekey  State key that's true once every one that's `required` is allowed
  title        any  Over them
  children: no
ui-photo-annotate: Marks on a photo: arrows, boxes, circles, freehand, text, measurements and blurring (for faces and number plates), kept apart from the picture and drawn onto a copy of it.
  src          any (required)  The picture: an address or `data:`; may use state. An object with a `url` (a `ui-camera` photo) will do
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the picture with the marks drawn on it (a `data:` address) as they change
  bindMarks    statekey  State key for the marks: `[{ id, type, points, text, color }]`, points as parts of the picture, 0 to 1
  tools        any  Which, in order: `[select, arrow, box, circle, pen, text, measure, blur]` (default all)
  colors       any  Default red, amber, green, blue, white and black
  width        number  Of the lines, in px of a 1000 px wide picture (default 6)
  unit         any  For measurements, e.g. `cm`: the first one's length is typed, and the others are worked out from it (default `cm`)
  type         one of: jpeg, png, webp  Default `jpeg`
  quality      number  0 to 1 (default 0.85)
  maxSize      number  The result's longer side at most, in px (default 2000)
  readonly     bool  The marks are shown, not changed
  label        any  Names it (default `Mark up the photo`)
  children: no
ui-location: Where the device is, once or as it moves, with how accurate that is; typed instead where it can't be found.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, accuracy, altitude, heading, speed, at }`, the accuracy in metres
  watch        bool  Follows the device as it moves, while the page is open
  auto         bool  Found by itself, where it's been allowed
  precise      bool  With GPS rather than a quick guess (default true)
  enough       number  Metres: keeps trying for a while until it's as accurate as this
  manual       bool  Can be typed instead
  link         any  Where its Open in maps goes, with `{lat}` and `{lng}` (default OpenStreetMap); null for none
  label        any  The button (default `Use my location`)
  children: no
ui-field-map: A light map to move and zoom, drawn without a library: markers (grouped when they're close), areas, lines, where the device is, and drawing on it.
  center       any  `{ lat, lng }` or `[lat, lng]`; may use state, and the map follows it (default: what's on it)
  zoom         any  0 (the world) to 19 (a building); may use state
  markers      any  `[{ id, lat, lng, label, text, color, glyph }]`: `text` is shown when it's picked, `glyph` is a character in the pin
  areas        any  `[{ id, points: [[lat, lng]], label, color }]`, or a circle: `{ lat, lng, radius }`, in metres
  lines        any  `[{ id, points, color, width, dashed, label }]`
  cluster      bool  Markers near each other are one, with their number, until zoomed in
  bindSelected statekey  State key for the id of the marker, area or line picked
  bindView     statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, zoom, bounds: [[south, west], [north, east]] }` as it's moved
  bindPoint    statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng }` where the map was clicked
  bindDrawn    statekey  State key for what's drawn on it: `[{ id, type, points, radius }]`
  draw         any  What can be drawn: `[marker, line, polygon, circle]`
  locate       bool  A button shows where the device is
  position     any  A dot at `{ lat, lng, accuracy, heading }`, e.g. what `ui-location` gives
  fit          bool  Starts with everything on it in view (default true, without `center`)
  height       any  Default 360 px
  tiles        any  Tiles' address, with `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`; `none` for a plain ground (default OpenStreetMap's, which are for light use: name your own for an app)
  attribution  any  Whose map it is (default `© OpenStreetMap contributors`)
  darkTiles    bool  In dark mode the tiles are turned dark (default true)
  wheel        bool  The wheel zooms without Ctrl or ⌘
  minZoom      number  Default 1
  maxZoom      number  Default 19
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Map`)
  children: no
ui-geo-checkin: Checks in and out where someone has to be: how far they are from the place, the time, how long it's been, and a photo. Children (a `ui-camera`, say) go before the button. A device can be made to lie about where it is, so it's a record, not proof.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the visit that's open, `{ id, place, in: { at, lat, lng, accuracy, distance, inside, reason, photo } }` (null when there's none)
  places       any (required)  Where one can check in: `[{ id, name, lat, lng, radius }]`, metres, or `points` for an area; may use state
  bindLog      statekey  State key that collects the visits that have ended, with `out` and `seconds`
  outside      one of: block, reason, allow  Away from every place: not at all (default), with a reason, or allowed
  enough       number  The least accuracy that counts, in metres (default 100)
  ready        any  The button waits for this, e.g. `{{ photo != null }}`
  photo        any  Kept with it, e.g. `{{ photo }}`
  inLabel      any  Default `Check in`
  outLabel     any  Default `Check out`
  children: yes
ui-route-tracker: Records a path while the app is open and in front: distance, time and speed, with pause, and GPX to save. Draw it on a `ui-field-map`, and keep it with `ui-local-store`.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the route, `{ state: idle|recording|paused|done, points: [[lat, lng, time, accuracy]], distance, seconds, started, ended }`, metres
  step         number  Metres between points at least (default 10)
  enough       number  Points less accurate than this are left out, in metres (default 50)
  units        one of: metric, imperial  Default `metric`
  awake        bool  Keeps the screen on while it records (default true): a phone stops saying where it is once it sleeps
  download     string  A button saves it as GPX under this name, e.g. `route.gpx`
  children: no
ui-compass: Which way the device faces, and the way to a place from where one is. A phone's magnet is easily put off by metal.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets the heading, degrees from north
  heading      any  Or shown from this, e.g. a vehicle's or the wind's
  target       any  `{ lat, lng }` to point to, from `from`
  from         any  Where one is, e.g. what `ui-location` gives
  size         number  In px (default 220)
  children: no
ui-level: A spirit level from the device's own sensors, set to zero against a surface known to be level.
  bind         statekey  State key that gets `{ x, y, level }`, degrees off level
  value        any  Or shown from this `{ x, y }`
  tolerance    number  Degrees that count as level (default 0.5)
  mode         one of: surface, edge, auto  Lying on a surface, stood on an edge, or whichever it is (default `auto`)
  size         number  In px (default 220)
  children: no
ui-push-opt-in: Offers notifications at a good moment, says why, then asks; subscribes to pushes and sends the subscription to a server, by topic. The app's service worker (`irender app`) shows them.
  publicKey    any  The server's VAPID public key; without it, only the app's own notifications are allowed for, with no pushes
  saveUrl      any  The subscription and topics are POSTed here as JSON, `{ subscription, topics }`, and again as they change; `subscription` is null once they're off
  topics       any  What can be chosen: `[{ value, label, description, on }]`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets `{ state, topics, endpoint }`; `state`: on, off, denied, install (an iPhone, until the app's on the home screen) or unsupported
  title        any  Default `Stay up to date`
  text         any  Why, before the browser asks
  label        any  The button (default `Turn on notifications`)
  when         any  Waits for a good moment, e.g. `{{ ordered }}`: shown once this is true
  remember     string  A Not now button, which keeps it away for `days` in this browser, under this name
  days         number  Default 30
  test         bool  Once on, a button shows one
  children: no
ui-app-badge: A number on the installed app's icon, and in the tab's title. Draws nothing.
  count        any (required)  The number; none at 0, and a dot for `true`; may use state
  title        bool  Before the page's title too, as `(3) Inbox` (default true)
  children: no
ui-share: Shares a link, text or files with the device's own sheet; where there's none, a list: copy, email, download and others.
  url          any  A link (default the page's when there's nothing else); may use state
  title        any  May use state
  text         any  May use state
  files        any  Files to share: `[{ url, name, type }]`, e.g. `ui-camera` photos; may use state
  label        any  Default `Share`
  variant      one of: primary, outline, ghost  Default `outline`
  targets      any  Besides copying and email, where there's no share sheet: `[{ label, href }]`, with `{url}`, `{title}` and `{text}` in `href`
  sheet        one of: auto, own  `own` always shows the list, not the device's sheet (default `auto`)
  children: no

ui-offline-queue: Keeps what's sent without a connection (submits, forms and uploads) and sends it once there is one, in order, even after the app's been closed. Shows what's waiting and what was refused. Each is sent with an `x-queued-id` header, so a server can tell one it has had.
  paths        any  Addresses whose requests are kept, e.g. `[/api/inspections]`: any under them (default every one on the site)
  methods      any  Default `[POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE]`
  labels       any  What to call them: `{ /api/inspections: Inspection }`
  labelField   string  A field of what's sent that says which, e.g. `title`
  variant      one of: list, badge, none  Default `list`
  bind         statekey  State key that gets what's waiting: `[{ id, label, url, method, at, status, error, tries }]`
  bindCount    statekey  State key that gets how many
  retryEvery   number  Seconds between tries while the page is open (default 60)
  title        any  Over the list (default `Waiting to be sent`)
  emptyText    any  Default `Everything has been sent`
  hideEmpty    bool  Nothing is shown when there's nothing waiting
  children: no
ui-local-store: Keeps state keys on the device between visits. Draws nothing. Not for secrets: anyone with the device can read them.
  keys         any (required)  State keys to keep, e.g. `[draft, filters]`
  name         string  What they're kept under (default the page's address)
  where        one of: device, session  `device` (default) until cleared, `session` until the tab's closed
  maxAge       number  Days after which they're let go (default never)
  version      any  What's kept under another one is let go
  sync         bool  Other tabs follow (default true)
  bindReady    statekey  State key that's true once what was kept has been put back
  bindSaved    statekey  State key that gets the time they were last kept
  clear        any  When this becomes true, what's kept is let go
  children: no
ui-data-source: Says how one kind of record is fetched by id (people, items, accounts), for `expand` on tables and queries. Ids asked for together are fetched together, each once, and kept in memory for `ttl`. Draws nothing.
  name         string (required)  What queries and tables call it in `expand`, e.g. `people`
  key          string  The field that holds a record's id (default `id`)
  batch        any  Many ids in one call: `{ url, method, param, style, params, body, max, pick }`. GET (default) sends `<url>?ids=1,2,3` (`param` names it; `style: repeat` sends `ids=1&ids=2`); POST sends `{ ids: [...] }` with `body`'s fields. At most `max` ids a call (default 50). The answer is a list of records or a map by id, at `pick` (default the answer, or its `rows`, `data` or `items`)
  one          string  One id a call, where there's no `batch`: GET `<url>` with `{id}` in it, e.g. `/api/people/{id}`; 404 means there's none
  pick         string  With `one`: the record's path in the answer, e.g. `data`
  ttl          number  Seconds a record is kept before it's fetched again (default 300); it's shown meanwhile
  missingTtl   number  Seconds an id with no record is remembered as none before it's asked for again (default `ttl`)
  concurrency  number  Calls at a time (default 4)
  wait         number  Milliseconds to gather ids before calling (default 0: what's asked for in the same turn)
  headers      any  Request headers, e.g. `{ x-tenant: acme }`
  persist      one of: memory, device  `memory` (default): for the page's life; `device`: kept on the device too (IndexedDB), shown first and when offline
  scope        any  With `device`: whose records these are, e.g. `{{ user.id }}`; another one lets the others go from the page, and they're kept apart
  private      any  Fields kept on the device only encrypted, with the key a `ui-app-lock` unlocks (none: they aren't kept), e.g. `[email, phone]`
  retain       number  Days private fields may stay on the device without being fetched again (default 30)
  version      any  With `device`: the shape of what's kept, e.g. `2`; what was kept under another one is let go (a changed API, say)
  maxAge       number  With `device`: days what's kept may be shown before it's let go (default: no limit)
  maxRecords   number  With `device`: at most this many records kept on the device, those fetched longest ago let go first (default: no limit)
  clear        any  When this becomes true, its records (of `scope`, or every one without) are let go from the device and the page, e.g. `{{ !user }}`
  write        any  Changes made here, also offline: `{ url, create, method, version, conflict }`. A `submit` to `url` (`/api/people/{id}`: PATCH, PUT or POST changes, DELETE deletes) or `create` (POST) changes the record at once and is sent when there's a connection, with the version it was made on: `If-Match` with the record's ETag (`version: etag`, default), or a field (`version: version`) sent in the body too. A 409 or 412 is settled by `conflict`: `merge` (default: both sides' changes, asking only about a field both changed), `server-wins`, `client-wins` or `ask`
  bindWrites   statekey  State key that gets this source's changes not yet saved: `[{ id, record, kind, status, error, changes, fields }]`, status waiting, sending, conflict or refused
  children: no
ui-data-query: Fills a state key with rows from an API, or with records by id, joined to the records they name (`expand`), for a chart, a list or any component. The rows come first; joined fields follow as their records arrive. Draws nothing.
  into         statekey (required)  State key that gets the rows (or the record, for one id)
  url          any  GET this for the rows; may use state, and a change loads again. The answer is a list, `{ rows, total }`, or one record
  params       any  Query parameters for `url`; blank ones are left out, and a change loads again
  pick         string  Path to the rows in the answer (default the answer, or its `rows`, `data` or `items`)
  source       string  Instead of `url`: the records of this `ui-data-source` for `ids`
  ids          any  With `source`: an id (into gets the record) or a list (the records); may use state
  expand       any  Joins records into each row: `{ owner: { source: people, from: ownerId } }` puts the `people` record whose id is in `ownerId` in `owner` (`from` may hold a list of ids). While it's on its way the row's `$loading.owner` is true; `$failed.owner` when it couldn't be fetched
  records      string  With `url`: the rows are this `ui-data-source`'s records (by its `key`), so changes written to them here show in the rows at once: changed, gone when deleted, and new ones at the end, until the rows are loaded again
  status       statekey  State key that gets `{ state, pending, total, error, at }`: state is idle, loading, joining (rows here, joined records on their way), ready or error
  refresh      any  Loads again when this changes, e.g. `{{ saved }}`
  paused       any  Nothing is loaded while true
  headers      any  Request headers for `url`
  persist      one of: memory, device  `memory` (default): for the page's life; `device`: kept on the device too (IndexedDB), shown first and when offline
  scope        any  With `device`: whose records these are, e.g. `{{ user.id }}`; another one lets the others go from the page, and they're kept apart
  private      any  Fields kept on the device only encrypted, with the key a `ui-app-lock` unlocks (none: they aren't kept), e.g. `[email, phone]`
  retain       number  Days private fields may stay on the device without being fetched again (default 30)
  version      any  With `device`: the shape of what's kept, e.g. `2`; what was kept under another one is let go (a changed API, say)
  maxAge       number  With `device`: days what's kept may be shown before it's let go (default: no limit)
  keep         number  With `device`: answers kept for this `url` (one per set of `params`), those loaded longest ago let go first (default 50)
  sync         any  Asks only for what changed since the last answer: `true` or `{ param, cursor, deleted, tombstone, key, full }`. The answer's `cursor` (default `cursor`) is sent back as `?since=` (`param`); its rows replace those with the same `key` (default `id`) or are added, and rows whose `tombstone` field (default `deleted`) is true, or whose ids are in its `deleted` list, go. Everything is loaded again every `full` hours (default 24)
  every        number  Seconds between loads while the page is in sight (at least 5); it also loads when the connection comes back
  clear        any  When this becomes true, the answers kept for `scope` are let go and the rows emptied, and nothing loads while it stays true, e.g. `{{ !user }}`
  children: no
ui-data-conflicts: Changes made here that the server changed too, to settle field by field (yours or theirs), and changes it refused, to dismiss: for a `ui-data-source` with `write` and `conflict: ask` (or a field both changed with `merge`).
  source       string  Only this `ui-data-source`'s (default every one's)
  labels       any  Fields' names to show, e.g. `{ phone: Phone }` (default the field)
  nameField    string  The record's field that names it, e.g. `name` (default its id)
  title        any  Default `Changed by someone else`
  emptyText    any  Shown when there's nothing to settle (default: it hides)
  children: no
ui-app-shell: An app's frame: a bar with the screen's title and a Back button, the screen, and tabs at the foot (down the side with room for them), clear of a phone's notch. Children are `ui-app-screen`s and one `ui-app-actions`, at the end of the bar.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the screen shown, a `ui-app-screen`'s `value`
  title        any  In the bar (default the screen's own)
  height       any  Default the window's; px or a CSS length
  rail         bool  With room for it, the tabs go down the side (default true)
  bar          bool  The bar at the top (default true)
  pullToRefresh bool  Pulling the screen down runs `on: { refresh: … }`
  bindRefreshing statekey  State key that pulling sets to true; set it to false once it's done (default: it stops by itself)
  history      bool  The browser's and the phone's back button go back through the screens
  label        any  Names the tabs for screen readers (default `Main`)
  parts: bar, main, tabs
  children: yes

  icon         any  Its tab's: an icon name (with the icon kit) or a character

ui-filters: Filters for a list: a button that opens a side panel of fields, each with its operators, and the applied filters as chips. Writes `{ field: condition }` to `bind`, for a chart's or data table's `filter`. Children are `ui-filter`s.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the applied filters, `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-chart`'s `filter`
  rows         any  Rows the filters are for, e.g. `{{ orders }}`: list filters without `options` offer their field's values, each with a count
  title        any  The panel's heading (default `Filters`)
  label        any  The button's text (default `Filters`)
  live         bool  Apply each change at once, with no Apply button
  chips        bool  Show the applied filters as chips beside the button (default true)
  currency     string  Currency code for `currency` filters, e.g. `INR` (default `USD`)
  locale       string  Locale for numbers and dates in chips (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  bindViews    statekey  State key for saved views, `[{ name, filters }]`: a Views menu applies, saves and deletes them
  today        string  The date date presets count from (default: today)
  searchFields bool  A box over the fields that finds one by its name or section (default: on past eight fields)
  fiscalStart  number  The month a financial year starts, 1–12 (default 1): the quarter and year presets follow it
  id           any  The panel's element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: button, panel
  children: yes
ui-filter: One field of the `ui-filters` it is in: its type, label and operators. Read by `ui-filters`, never rendered on its own.
  field        string (required)  The rows' field it filters
  label        any  Its name in the panel and chips (default: the field)
  type         one of: list, number, currency, date, text  `list` (default): values to pick; `number`, `currency`, `date` or `text`
  options      any  A list filter's values: text, or `{ value, label }`. May use state. Default: the field's values in the filters' `rows`
  optionsUrl   any  A list filter's values from an API as they're searched for: GET `<url>?q=<text>`, answering texts or `{ value, label, count }`s. May use state
  operators    any  Which operators to offer, by name, e.g. `[between, before, after]` (default: all of the type's)
  section      string  A heading to group it under in the panel
  unit         string  Shown after a number, e.g. `kg`
  currency     string  This filter's currency, over the filters' `currency`
  presets      any  A date filter's quick ranges: `true` (default: today, yesterday, last7, last30, thisMonth, lastMonth, thisQuarter, thisYear), `false`, or a list of those names
  children: no
ui-tree: A tree of nodes to browse, select, check, search, add to, delete from and rearrange by dragging or with Alt and the arrow keys. Nodes can be renamed in place (`renamable`), carry an `icon`, and load their children from an API when first opened (`childrenUrl`). Changes go to state (`bindNodes`) and fire `select`, `add`, `delete`, `move` and `rename` events.
  nodes        any (required)  The nodes: `{ id, label (or name), icon, children }`, usually from state, e.g. `{{ locations }}`
  bindNodes    statekey  State key the nodes are in: moves and deletions are written back to it
  bind         statekey  State key for the selected node's id
  bindNode     statekey  State key for the selected node itself, to show its fields beside the tree
  checkable    bool  A checkbox per node; checking a node checks the nodes under it
  bindChecked  statekey  State key for the checked nodes' ids
  addable      bool  An Add button, and one on each node. With `bindNodes` they ask for a name and add the node; either way they write the parent's id (null for the top) to `bindParent` and fire `add`
  bindParent   statekey  State key that gets the parent's id when Add is pressed
  deletable    bool  A delete button on each node, Delete on the keyboard, and Delete for the checked nodes
  movable      bool  Drag nodes to a new place, or move the focused one with Alt and the arrow keys
  renamable    bool  Rename a node in place: F2, or a double click on its name
  childrenUrl  any  Loads a node's children when it's first opened, for nodes with `children: true`: GET with `?parent=<id>`, answering a list of nodes (or `{ nodes }`)
  search       any  A search box above the tree: `true`, or its placeholder. Shows matches with the nodes above them
  counts       bool  Show how many nodes are under each node
  expanded     any  Open to start with: `true` for every node, a number of levels, or a list of ids (default: the selected node's parents)
  icons        any  Icon names nodes loaded later may use (from `childrenUrl` or state), so the icon kit draws them
  title        any  A heading above the tree, which also names it for screen readers
  label        any  Names the tree for screen readers when there's no `title` (default `Tree`)
  addLabel     any  The Add button's text (default `Add`)
  emptyText    any  Shown when there are no nodes (default `Nothing here yet.`)
  height       any  Most it grows to before it scrolls: a number (px) or CSS length
  parts: tree
  children: no
ui-file-upload: Files to attach: a drop zone, uploads with progress, the files as a grid or a list, a preview of images, PDFs, spreadsheets and text, and Download all as a zip. The files are kept in state under `bind`.

  url          any  Where to upload: each file is POSTed as `multipart/form-data` (field `file`), and a JSON answer is merged into its entry, e.g. `{ id, url }`. Without it, files stay in the browser
  params       any  More form fields sent with each file, e.g. `{ folder: "{{ claim.id }}" }`

  hint         any  Smaller text under it, e.g. the types and size allowed
  readOnly     bool  Show the files only: no drop zone and no removing
  removable    bool  A remove button on each file (default true)
  download     bool  A Download all button that saves the files as one zip (default true)
  zipName      string  The zip's name, without `.zip` (default `attachments`)
  emptyText    any  Shown under a read-only list with no files (default `No files yet.`)
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  id           any  The file input's id, for a label (default: derived from the document)

  children: no

ui-countdown: The time left to a deadline, turning to warning and danger as thresholds pass and counting up once overdue; as text or tiles, with a bar of the time used.
  to           any (required)  The deadline: a date and time (`2026-12-01T17:00`, `2026-12-01T17:00:00Z`), milliseconds, or `+7h 40m` from when the page opens; may use state
  from         any  When the time started, as `to` (`-16h 20m`: before the page opened): a bar shows how much of it is used
  warn         any  Time left when it turns to the warning tone: seconds, or `90s`, `30m`, `4h`, `2d`
  danger       any  Time left when it turns to the danger tone, as `warn`
  overdue      bool  Past the deadline, count up as overdue (default true); false shows `endText`
  endText      any  Shown once it's over, with `overdue: false` (default `Time's up`)
  format       one of: units, clock  `units` (default: `2d 4h`, `13m 05s`) or `clock` (`2:04:13`, `3d 02:04:13`)
  variant      one of: inline, tiles  `inline` (default: text with a dot in its tone) or `tiles` (days, hours, minutes and seconds in boxes)
  paused       any  While true (e.g. `{{ ticket.status == 'waiting' }}`), the time left stands still and it says Paused; on resuming the deadline moves out by the pause. A new `to` from the page replaces the moved one
  workdays     any  Count working time only: `true` for Monday to Friday, or the weekdays that work (0 is Sunday), e.g. `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`
  hours        any  Working hours each working day, e.g. `09:00-17:30` (local time); outside them it stands still. Alone, every day works
  holidays     any  Dates that don't count either, e.g. `["2026-12-25"]`
  bindLeft     statekey  State key that gets the seconds left (below zero once overdue), every second
  bindStatus   statekey  State key that gets `ok`, `warning`, `danger` or `over` as it changes
  label        any  What it counts down to, for screen readers, e.g. `First reply due`
  children: no

ui-approval: A sign-off in stages, each approved when its rule is met: who decided what, when and why; Approve, Request changes and Reject on your turn.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the stages, in order: `{ id, title, rule, due, approvers: [{ id, name, avatar, decision, comment, at, for }], rounds }`; `rule` is `all` (default), `any` or a number, `decision` approved, changes or rejected, `due` a date it's due by, `for` the approver who handed it on, `rounds` earlier rounds' approvers (kept when it's sent again)
  me           any  The `id` of whoever's looking: on their turn, they get the buttons to decide
  owner        any  The `id` of whoever sent it: after changes or a rejection, they can send it again
  bindStatus   statekey  State key that gets `pending`, `changes`, `rejected` or `approved`, as it changes

  children: no
ui-scheduler: Bookings against time, a row per person, room, vehicle or machine: moved, stretched and made by dragging or the keys, with clashes marked.
  resources    any (required)  The rows: `[{ id, title, subtitle, avatar, group, hours: [{ from, to }], capacity }]`; may use state
  events       any (required)  The bookings: `[{ id, resource, title, start, end, color, status, locked, note }]`, times as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`; `repeat`, as `ui-event-calendar`'s, makes one come again (its days aren't moved one by one); may use state
  bindEvents   statekey  State key the bookings are in: moves, stretches and new ones are written back

ui-import: Rows from a spreadsheet (CSV, Excel, or pasted cells): its columns are matched to `fields`, the rows put right in an editable table, and the good ones handed over (an `import` event and `bindImported`) or posted to `url`.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the rows while they're reviewed
  bindImported statekey  State key that gets the rows that passed, once imported (or sent)
  fields       any (required)  What each row has: `[{ field, label, type, options, required, min, max, pattern, unique, message, aliases, example, format }]`; `type`: text, multiline, number, date, select or checkbox; `aliases`: other names its column may have
  url          any  Post the rows here in batches, `{ rows }` as JSON; answering `{ errors: [{ row, field, message }] }` (`row` counts from 0 in the batch) sends those back to be put right
  params       any  With `url`, more to send with each batch; may use state
  batchSize    number  With `url`, rows per request (default 200)
  accept       string  File types (default `.csv,.tsv,.txt,.xlsx`)
  maxRows      number  The most rows a file may have (default 10000)
  skipInvalid  bool  Rows that aren't right can be left out (default true; false: all must be right)
  template     any  Offers an empty file to fill in: `true` (default), its name ending in `.csv` or `.xlsx`, or false
  title        any  Names what's imported, e.g. `Contacts` (default `Rows`)
  locale       string  How numbers and dates are read (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  children: no
ui-form: A form whose fields are checked by `rules` as they're left and when it's submitted (`on: { submit: … }` runs only when all is right), which knows its unsaved changes. A `remote` rule asks the server (is this name taken?). Put a `ui-error-summary` and a `ui-save-bar` in it.
  rules        any  What each state key must be: `{ email: { label, required, type: email|url|number|date, min, max, minLength, maxLength, pattern, match: otherKey, message, remote } }`. Any of them may use state, e.g. `required: "{{ kind == 'company' }}"`. `remote: /api/available` (or `{ url, param, wait, message, headers }`) asks the server once the other rules pass, `wait` ms (default 400) after the value last changed: GET `url?value=…` (`param` renames it; `{value}` in the url is replaced instead), answered by `true`, `{ valid: true }`, or what's wrong (`false`, a text, `{ valid: false, message }`). A submit waits for it; if the server can't be reached the value passes (it's checked again when sent) and the form fires `failed`
  bindErrors   statekey  State key that gets `{ key: message }` for the fields left so far (all of them once submitting was tried); give it to each `ui-field`'s `error`
  bindValid    statekey  State key that gets true while every rule is met (not while a `remote` one is being asked)
  bindChecking statekey  State key that gets the keys whose `remote` rule is being asked, e.g. for a field's `description: "{{ includes(checking, 'handle') ? 'Checking…' : '' }}"`
  bindTried    statekey  State key that gets true once submitting was tried with something wrong
  keys         any  State keys whose changes are unsaved changes (default: those with `rules`)
  bindDirty    statekey  State key that gets true while there are unsaved changes; set it to false once saved (a `submit` that succeeds does)
  guard        bool  Asks before leaving the page with unsaved changes
  guardText    any  What's asked (default `You have unsaved changes that will be lost.`)
  disabled     any  Nothing can be changed or submitted, e.g. `{{ saving }}`
  columns      number  Lays what's in it out in columns, 1–6; two and then one as it narrows. Children take more with `span` (`ui-field`, `ui-form-section`) or `style: { grid-column: 1 / -1 }`
  children: yes
ui-error-summary: What's wrong in the `ui-form` it's in, listed once submitting was tried; each message goes to its field.
  title        any  Default `There's a problem` / `There are {n} problems`
  errors       any  More messages than the form's own, e.g. from the server: `{ key: message }` or a list of texts
  children: no
ui-save-bar: Shown while the `ui-form` it's in has unsaved changes: Save submits the form, Discard puts its fields back. Children go before the buttons.
  text         any  Default `Unsaved changes`
  saveLabel    any  The button that submits the form (default `Save`)
  discardLabel any  The button that puts the fields back as they were (default `Discard`); false for none
  saving       any  Being saved: both buttons wait, e.g. `{{ saving }}`
  disabled     any  It can't be saved as it is, e.g. `{{ problems.length > 0 }}`; Discard still works
  position     one of: sticky, fixed, inline  Default `sticky`, at the foot of the window while the form is on it
  children: yes
ui-form-section: A titled group of fields, with columns of its own. Sections go in a `ui-form` (which may have `columns` too, to put sections side by side) or in each other; children take more columns with `span`.
  title        any  Its heading
  description  any  Text under the heading
  columns      number  Columns for what's in it, 1–6 (default 1); two and then one as it narrows
  layout       one of: stacked, aside  The heading above the fields (default), or `aside`: beside them (up to 240px wide) while there's room
  span         any  Columns it takes in the form or section it's in: a number or `full`
  level        any  Its heading's level, 2–6 (default 3)
  collapsible  bool  Folds under its heading, which opens and closes it (needs a `title`); the form opens it to go to a field inside
  open         any  With `collapsible`: starts open (default true)
  bindOpen     statekey  With `collapsible`, a state key that's true while it's open, both ways (it starts as the key says)
  children: yes

  bind         statekey (required)  State key holding the rows, a list of objects
  fields       any (required)  The fields of a row: `[{ field, label, type, options, placeholder, width, required, min, max, pattern, unique, message, default, compute, format, currency, decimals, summary }]`. `type`: text, multiline, number, currency, date, time, email, tel, url, select, combobox (typed, picked from `options` as you type), checkbox, or computed (`compute: qty * price`, over the row's fields and state)
  layout       one of: table, stack  `table` (default): one line per row under a header (stacked on a narrow screen); `stack`: a card per row with labels

  showErrors   any  When to show messages: after a field was left (default), or true for all, e.g. `{{ tried }}`

  children: yes
ui-kanban: A board of columns with cards to drag between them (or move with Alt and the arrow keys), add to, and open. The new order goes to `bindCards`, with `move`, `add` and `open` events. Children, if any, are each card's content, with the card as `card` (and its place in its cell as `index`).
  columns      any (required)  The columns, in order: `{ id, title, tone, limit }` (or plain names). `limit` marks a column over it
  cards        any (required)  The cards, in order: `{ id, column, title, description, tags, assignee, due, priority }`, usually from state, e.g. `{{ tasks }}`
  bindCards    statekey  State key the cards are in: moves and new cards are written back to it
  bindCard     statekey  State key that gets the card clicked or opened with Enter
  movable      bool  Drag cards, or move the focused one with Alt and the arrow keys (default true)
  addable      bool  An Add card button under each column, which asks for a title (needs `bindCards`)
  collapsible  bool  A button on each column to fold it away
  collapsed    any  Columns folded to start with, by id
  addLabel     any  The add button's text (default `Add card`)
  emptyText    string  In a column with no cards (default `No cards`)
  columnWidth  number  Each column's width in px (default 280)
  label        any  Names the board for screen readers (default `Board`)
  swimlanes    string  A card field to split the board by: a row of columns per value, e.g. `assignee`; moving a card to a lane writes it. May use state (null: no lanes)
  lanes        any  With `swimlanes`, the lanes in order: values or `{ value, label }` (default: the values as cards have them)
  fields       any  More of each card, a line each: `{ field, label, cell }`, `cell` being `text` (default), `badge` (with `tones`), `progress` (0–100) or `date`. May use state, e.g. a list picked by a setting
  reorderable  bool  A grip on each column's header moves the column: dragged, or Left and Right on it (with `bindColumns`); with lanes, one on each lane's header moves the lane, or Up and Down (with `bindLanes`)
  bindColumns  statekey  State key the columns are in: a moved column's new order is written back to it
  bindLanes    statekey  State key `lanes` reads: a moved lane's new order is written back to it
  locale       string  Locale for `date` fields (default: the document's `lang`)
  filter       any  Shows only the cards that pass: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-data-table`'s and `ui-chart`'s `filter`, e.g. a `ui-filters` panel's `bind`. Applied in the browser
  parts: board
  children: yes
ui-event-calendar: Events in a month grid, a week of hours, or a list by day, coloured by category, with a toolbar to move through time. Clicks go to `bindEvent` (an event) and `bindDay` (a day, e.g. to add one).
  events       any (required)  The events: `{ id, title, start, end, allDay, category, tone, description }`, with `start` and `end` as dates (`2026-11-04`) or local times (`2026-11-04T09:30`). `repeat` makes one come again: `{ every: day|week|month|year, interval, on: [1, 3] (weekdays, 0 is Sunday), until, count, except: [dates] }`
  view         one of: day, week, month, year, list  The view to start in: `day`, `week`, `month` (default), `year` or `list`
  views        any  Which views to offer, in order (default all five: day, week, month, year, list); one hides the switch
  date         any  The day to show to start with (default today)
  days         any  Marks on days, apart from events: `[{ date, end, tone, label, items, repeat }]` (or a map of date → `{ tone, label, items }`). `tone` shades the day, `label` is written beside its date, and `items` are small badges under it (text, or `{ text, tone, id }`; one with an `id` is a button firing `badge`); `end` makes it a run of days, and `repeat` repeats it as an event's does (`week` with `on: [0]`, every Sunday)
  yearEvents   bool  The year view tints days with events (default true); false tints only the `days` with a tone
  categories   any  Category → tone (`info`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `primary`, `neutral`), shown as a legend
  bindEvent    statekey  State key that gets the event clicked
  bindEvents   statekey  State key holding the events: makes them movable (drag them, or Alt and the arrow keys) and writes the list back
  snap         number  Minutes a move or a resize snaps to (default 15)
  bindDay      statekey  State key that gets the day picked (`2026-11-04`), e.g. to add an event on it
  bindBadge    statekey  State key that gets a badge clicked (one of `days`' items with an `id`), `{ date, item }`, as `badge` fires
  bindView     statekey  State key that gets the view when it changes
  hours        any  The week view's hours, `[from, to]` (default `[7, 20]`)
  weekStart    number  0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday (default)
  maxPerDay    number  Events shown in a month's day before `+N more` (default 3)
  today        string  The date to treat as today (default: the real one)
  locale       string  Locale for dates and times (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  emptyText    any  The list view's text for a month with nothing in it
  label        any  Names it for screen readers (default `Calendar`)
  parts: toolbar
  children: no
ui-number-input: A number or an amount, grouped as it's typed (`1,25,000`), with a currency symbol, prefix or suffix, Up and Down to step it, and optional − and + buttons. State gets a plain number.
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the number (null when empty)
  currency     string  An ISO currency code, e.g. `INR`: its symbol goes before the number, and its decimals apply
  prefix       any  Text before the number, e.g. `~` (instead of a currency's symbol)
  suffix       any  Text after the number, e.g. `kg` or `%`
  locale       string  How the number is written, e.g. `en-IN` (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  min          number  The smallest it can be; leaving the field raises it to this
  max          number  The largest it can be
  step         number  How much Up, Down and the buttons change it (default 1)
  decimals     number  Digits after the decimal point (default: the currency's, or as typed)
  stepper      bool  − and + buttons beside it
  placeholder  any  Shown while it's empty
  label        any  Accessible name, when no visible label (such as a `ui-field`'s) names it
  name         string  Form field name
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  invalid      any  Mark it wrong, e.g. `{{ amount > budget }}`
  id           any  The input's id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: input
  children: no
ui-notifications: A bell with an unread count that opens a panel of notifications, with Unread and All, mark read or unread, archive and Mark all as read. Changes go to `bindItems`; a click opens one into `bindItem`.
  items        any (required)  The notifications, newest first: `{ id, title, body, who, when, read, archived, tone }`, with `who` a name or `{ name, initials, avatar }`
  bindItems    statekey  State key the items are in: read and archived are written back to it
  bindItem     statekey  State key that gets the notification clicked
  inline       bool  The panel in the page, with no bell (for a notifications page)
  tab          any  The tab to start in: `unread` (default) or `all`
  title        any  The panel's heading (default `Notifications`)
  label        any  Names the bell for screen readers (default `Notifications`)
  emptyText    any  With nothing at all (default `No notifications.`)
  caughtUp     any  In Unread with nothing unread (default `You're all caught up.`)
  allHref      any  A link under the list to every notification, e.g. `/notifications`
  closeOnOpen  bool  Close the panel when a notification is clicked (default true)
  parts: bell, panel
  children: no
ui-rail-layout: An app shell: a rail of icons, each opening its own panel beside it (`ui-rail-panel` children), and the main content after. The section shown is in `bind`, the panel's open state in `bindOpen`.
  items        any (required)  The rail's sections: `{ id, label, icon, badge, bottom, href }`. `icon` is an icon kit name or a character; `bottom` puts it at the foot; `href` makes it a link
  bind         statekey (required)  State key for the section shown (an item's `id`)
  bindOpen     statekey  State key for whether the panel is open (true or false): a click on the open section folds it
  label        any  Names the rail for screen readers (default `Sections`)
  panelWidth   number  The panel's width in px (default 260)
  resizable    bool  A handle on the panel's edge to drag it wider or narrower (or focus it and use the arrow keys)
  bindWidth    statekey  State key for the panel's width in px, written after each resize
  minPanelWidth number  The narrowest a resize makes it, in px (default 180)
  maxPanelWidth number  The widest a resize makes it, in px (default 560)
  height       any  The shell's height (default `100svh`)

  children: yes
ui-rail-panel: The panel a `ui-rail-layout` item opens: its children, under a heading. Read by the layout, never rendered on its own.

  title        any  A heading at its top
  children: yes
ui-resizable: Panels side by side or stacked (`ui-resizable-panel` children), with a handle between each two to resize them by dragging or with the arrow keys. Sizes are percentages; `bind` keeps them in state.
  direction    string  `horizontal` (side by side, the default) or `vertical` (stacked)
  bind         statekey  State key for the sizes: a list of percentages, one per panel, written after each move
  handle       bool  Shows a grip on each handle
  height       any  The group's height (default: as tall as its container lets it be)
  label        any  Names the handles for screen readers: `Resize <label>` (default `Resize panels`)
  parts: handle
  children: yes
ui-resizable-panel: One panel of a `ui-resizable`: its children, at its size. Read by the group, never rendered on its own.
  size         number  Its starting size in % (the panels without one share what's left)
  min          number  The smallest it can be, in % (default 10)
  max          number  The largest it can be, in % (default 100)
  collapsible  bool  Can fold to nothing: dragged under half its `min`, or Enter on its handle
  label        any  Its name, read with the handle before it
  children: yes
ui-code-block: Code, highlighted, with line numbers, marked lines and a copy button. `code` can come from state: an object shows as JSON.
  code         any (required)  The code. Anything not a string (an object from state, say) shows as JSON
  language     string  json, yaml, js (ts), rust, python, bash, html, css, sql or text (the default)
  title        any  A file name or caption in the bar above
  lineNumbers  bool  Numbers the lines

  children: no

ui-theme-option: Picks one choice of a theme option (`theme.options`), such as a palette or a corner radius, for every page, and remembers it in the browser.

ui-theme-colors: Colour inputs, typed as hex or picked: a primary and a second brand colour, each with an optional gradient end, and the backgrounds of the page, cards, popovers, dialogs, sheets and the sidebar for the mode showing. ui-combobox: A searchable select: one or many values, groups, async options, creatable values, full keyboard support.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the value (an array with `multiple`)
  options      any  Values, `{ value, label, description, disabled }`, or groups `{ label, options }`. From data, or a state path
  valueField   string  Field of an option object holding its value (default `value`)
  labelField   string  Field holding its label (default `label`)
  descriptionField string  Field holding its description (default `description`)

  loadingText  any  Default `Loading…`

  parts: control, input, menu
  children: no

ui-conversation: A scrolling chat log that keeps to its latest message as messages arrive, unless you've scrolled up to read; then a button jumps back down. Children are `ui-message`s, followed by `messages`. Its `parts.bubble`, `parts.avatar` and so on style the messages drawn from `messages`.
  messages     any  Array of messages, after any children. From state, like `{{ messages }}`, it redraws as it changes
  typing       any  Show a typing indicator after the last message, e.g. `{{ waiting }}`
  render       any  How messages' `ui` without `html` is rendered: `{ browser, url }`, as on `ui-message`
  markdown     bool  Show messages as Markdown, as on `ui-message` (default: when irender-markdown-kit is registered)
  assistant    any  The typing indicator's sender: `{ name, avatar, initials }`
  empty        any  Text shown while `messages` is empty
  label        any  Names the conversation for screen readers (default `Conversation`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length
  maxHeight    any  Number (px) or CSS length: grows with the messages up to this
  actions      any  Buttons under each message: `[copy, retry, edit, up, down]`; see `ui-message`
  parts: log, empty, latest, avatar, body, meta, bubble, ui, thread, replies
  children: yes
ui-message: One chat message: a bubble with the sender's avatar, name and time, and an optional thread of replies. Children go in the bubble after the text.
  role         one of: assistant, user, system  Who it's from: `assistant` (default, on the left), `user` (on the right) or `system` (centred)
  content      any  The text, as Markdown with `markdown` (headings, lists, code, tables, links); otherwise plain, line breaks kept
  markdown     bool  Show `content` as Markdown (default: when irender-markdown-kit is registered)
  streaming    any  The content is still arriving: Markdown formatting left open at its end shows as it will once closed
  name         any  Sender's name, shown above the bubble
  time         any  When it was sent, as text, shown after the name
  avatar       any  Avatar image URL
  initials     any  Shown in the avatar when there's no image
  html         any  UI after the text, rendered on a server: by `render_ui` (the CLI renders each message's `ui` into it), or `irender render --embed`. Shown only in trusted documents
  ui           any  UI after the text as an iRender document or node, for `render` to render when there's no `html`
  render       any  How a `ui` without `html` is rendered: `{ browser, url }`. `browser` is irender-wasm's `.wasm` file, to render it in the page; `url` is your server's render endpoint, which gets `{ ui }` and answers with the markup, used when there's no `browser` or it can't render it
  messageId    any  Its id, for `actions`
  actions      any  Buttons under it: `[copy, retry, edit, up, down]`. A `ui-chat-input` on the page does the rest: `retry` asks again, `edit` puts a message of yours back in the box, `up` and `down` write the message's `feedback`. Each fires `messageaction`
  feedback     any  `up` or `down`: which of the two is pressed
  sources      any  What it's based on, under it: as `ui-sources`' `items`
  attachments  any  Files sent with it, over it: as `ui-attachment`'s `files`
  replies      any  A thread: an array of messages shown under it, folded away behind `N replies`. May use state
  open         bool  Show the thread unfolded
  parts: avatar, body, meta, bubble, ui, thread, replies
  children: yes

  children: no
ui-chat-input: The box a chat message is written in. Enter sends and Shift+Enter starts a new line. Sending appends `{ id, role: user, content }` to `messages`, runs the document's `on.send` actions, and with `endpoint` asks it for the reply, streaming it into a new assistant message; while it streams, the send button stops it. With `threads` and `thread` it keeps a list of conversations. Children go in the toolbar, left of the send button.
  messages     statekey (required)  State key of the messages array: sending appends the user's message, and the reply
  endpoint     any  URL to POST `{ messages }` to. The reply may be JSON (a message, or `{ content }`), plain text, or server-sent events, which stream into the reply as they arrive
  body         any  More to send with each request, beside `messages`, e.g. `{ model: "{{ model }}" }`; may use state
  headers      any  Request headers, e.g. `{ authorization: "Bearer {{ token }}" }`; may use state
  bindFiles    statekey  State key of files to send with the next message (a `ui-file-upload`'s, or a `ui-attachment`'s): they become its `attachments`, and the key is emptied
  bind         statekey  State key holding the text being written
  waiting      statekey  State key set true from sending until the reply starts: give it to the conversation's `typing`
  threads      statekey  State key of an array of threads, `{ id, title, messages }`: the messages live in them, and `messages` shows the current one's. Needs `thread`
  thread       statekey  State key of the current thread's id; null for a new one, started by the first message
  placeholder  any  Default `Send a message…`
  label        any  Names the text box for screen readers (default `Message`)
  suggestions  any  Prompts shown while the conversation is empty; clicking one sends it
  disabled     any  Boolean or expression
  parts: suggestions, box, input, toolbar, send
  children: yes
ui-carousel: Slides in a row that scrolls sideways and snaps to each one: images, cards, anything. Its buttons, Left and Right on the focused track, and swiping move a slide at a time. Children are the slides.
  label        any  Names the carousel for screen readers (default `Carousel`)
  size         any  Each slide's width: number (px) or CSS length; default `min(280px, 85%)`
  gap          any  Space between slides: number (px) or CSS length; default 12
  dots         bool  A dot per slide under it, the current one marked; each goes to its slide
  loop         bool  Next at the end goes to the first slide, previous at the start to the last
  autoplay     number  Move on every this many ms, round and round, with a pause button; it waits while hovered or focused
  parts: track, previous, next, dots, play
  children: yes
ui-calendar: An inline calendar: days (with a time), months, quarters or years; one, a range or several; limits, presets, financial years and full keyboard support.
  bind         statekey  State key holding the value: `2026-03-01` (with `time`, `2026-03-01T14:30`; `2026-W09` (an ISO week), `2026-03`, `2026-Q1` or `2026` for the other pickers), `{ from, to }` with `mode: range` (with `time`, `{ from: 2026-03-02T09:00, to: 2026-03-06T17:00 }`), a list with `multiple`
  value        any  Starting value, when not bound
  picker       one of: day, week, month, quarter, year  What is picked: `day` (default), `week` (a whole week, Monday to Sunday, from the days), `month`, `quarter` or `year`
  mode         one of: single, range, multiple  `single` (default), `range` or `multiple`
  time         bool  A time as well as the day: one, or with `mode: range` a start and an end time (days only, not `multiple`)
  step         number  With `time`, minutes between times (default 1)
  min          any  Earliest date: `2026-01-01`, or `today`, `today-30d`, `today+1y`; may use state
  max          any  Latest date, as `min`
  disabledDates any  Dates that can't be picked: `2026-12-25`, or `{ from, to }`; may use state
  disabledDays any  Weekdays that can't be picked: 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday, e.g. `[0, 6]`
  months       number  Months shown side by side (default 1; 2 suits ranges)
  weekStart    number  First day of the week, 0 Sunday … 6 Saturday (default: the locale's)
  fiscalStart  number  Month a financial year starts, 1–12 (default 1); quarters and years follow it
  presets      any  Shortcuts beside the calendar: names (`last7`, `thisMonth`, `lastQuarter`, `yearToDate`, …) or `{ label, from, to }`
  dropdowns    bool  Month and year menus in place of the caption, for dates far away such as birthdays
  bindRange    statekey  State key that gets the dates the value covers, `{ from, to }`: a chart's or a table's filter
  compare      any  With `mode: range`, a period to compare with: `true`, or the kinds offered, from `previous`, `lastYear` and `custom`
  bindCompare  statekey  With `compare`, a state key holding the comparison, `{ type, from, to }` (the dates it covers), or null while it's off
  name         string  Form field name: hidden inputs carry the value (`name[from]` and `name[to]` for a range)
  locale       string  Locale for names and formats (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  label        any  Accessible name
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  clearable    bool  A Clear button under the calendar
  children: no
```
