```
ui-data-table: A data table: sorting, column filters, search, paging, row selection with bulk actions, expandable rows, a View menu and summaries. Children are `ui-data-table-column`s (a cell template, with the row as `row`), `ui-data-table-toolbar`, `ui-data-table-bulk` and `ui-data-table-detail`.
  rows         any  The rows: an array of objects, from data or state (or use `url`)
  url          any  Load rows from an API in batches: GET `<url>?offset=&limit=&sort=&q=&filters=`, answering `{ rows, total }` or an array. A query's first batch also asks `facets=` (select filters' fields) and `summary=` (`field:sum`, …); answering `facets: { field: [{ value, count }] }` and `summary: { "field:sum": n }` makes the filters and footer cover every matching row
  params       any  Extra query parameters for `url`; may use state, and a change reloads
  expand       any  Joins records from a `ui-data-source` into the rows drawn: `{ owner: { source: people, from: ownerId } }` puts the record whose id is in `ownerId` in `owner`, for columns like `owner.name`. Only the rows on the page are asked for, together; their cells pulse until it arrives
  columns      any  Columns as objects with the `ui-data-table-column` props, for tables with no cell templates
  rowKey       string  Field that identifies a row, for selection (default `id`; else its position)
  selectable   bool  A checkbox per row and a select-all box in the header
  search       any  A search box above the table: `true`, or its placeholder text
  searchFields any  Fields the search looks in (default: every column's field)
  sort         any  Starting sort: `field`, `-field` for descending, or a list of them
  filter       any  Filters from outside the table, e.g. a chart's `bind`: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-chart`'s `filter`
  paging       one of: pages, more, scroll, none  `pages` (default): a pager; `more`: a Load more button; `scroll`: the next batch as you reach the bottom; `none`
  pageSize     number  Rows per page, or per batch with `more` and `scroll` (default 10; 0 shows every row)
  childrenField string  Rows nest: the field holding a row's child rows (default `children`); `true` there means load them from `childrenUrl`
  parentField  string  Rows nest: flat rows name their parent's key in this field, e.g. `parentId`
  childrenUrl  any  Load a row's children when it's first opened: GET `<url>?parent=<key>`, answering an array or `{ rows }`
  expanded     bool  Nested rows start open (default false)
  selectChildren bool  Nested rows: picking a row picks the rows under it, and a row is picked when all under it are (default true)
  virtual      bool  Keep only the rows in view in the page, for long tables; scrolls inside `height` (default 480)
  rowHeight    number  With `virtual`, a row's height to start from before rows are measured (default 41)
  pageSizes    any  Choices for rows per page (default `[10, 20, 50, 100]`; `[]` hides it)
  columnsMenu  bool  A View menu that shows and hides columns (default true)
  groupBy      any  Groups the rows by this field, each group under a header row with its count and subtotals (may use state)
  bindGroupBy  statekey  State key holding the field the rows are grouped by (or null), set from the View menu
  resizable    bool  Columns can be made wider or narrower by dragging their header's edge
  reorderable  bool  Columns can be moved by dragging their header, or Alt and the arrow keys on it
  bindColumns  statekey  State key holding the columns' layout, `{ order, widths, hidden }`, to keep it
  export       any  An Export button that downloads the rows that pass the filters as CSV, or as Excel with a name ending in `.xlsx`: `true`, or the file's name
  title        any  Accessible name of the table
  emptyText    any  Shown when no row matches (default `No results.`)
  locale       string  Locale for formatted numbers and dates (default: the document's `lang`, else the browser's)
  height       any  Most the table grows to before it scrolls, with the header kept in view
  striped      bool  Shade every other row
  loading      any  Dim the rows and mark the table busy, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  bindSelection statekey  State key holding the selected rows' keys (a list)
  bindSort     statekey  State key holding the sort: `field`, `-field`, a list of them, or null
  bindFilters  statekey  State key holding the column filters, `{ field: condition }`: give it to a chart's `filter` to filter both
  bindSearch   statekey  State key holding the search text
  bindPage     statekey  State key holding the page number, from 1
  bindView     statekey  State key that gets the rows that pass the filters and search, sorted, every page: a chart's `data`
  bindRow      statekey  State key that gets the row last clicked (or opened with Enter)
  views        any  Ready-made views in a Views menu: `[{ id, name, sort, filters, search, columns, groupBy, pageSize }]`; they can't be changed or deleted
  bindViews    statekey  State key for the views people save from the Views menu (the same shape as `views`)
  bindCurrentView statekey  State key holding the id of the view shown (or null); the table opens with it
  defaultView  string  The view the table opens with when `bindCurrentView` has none
  editable     any  Which rows' cells can be edited (in columns with `edit`): true (default), or an expression over `row`, e.g. `{{ row.status != 'Closed' }}`
  addRow       any  Editable: a button under the rows that adds one: `true`, or its text. Rows pasted past the end are added too
  newRow       any  Editable: what an added row starts with, e.g. `{ status: Draft }`
  deletable    bool  Editable: Delete in the bulk bar removes the selected rows (turns on `selectable`)
  errors       any  Editable: messages to mark cells with, e.g. from the server: `{ rowKey: { field: message } }`
  bindErrors   statekey  Editable: state key that gets the cells that are wrong, `[{ key, field, message }]`
  bindChanges  statekey  Editable: state key that gets what changed, `{ rowKey: { field: value } }` (null for a deleted row); set it to `{}` once saved
  id           any  Element id (default: derived from the document)
  parts: toolbar, table, footer
  children: yes
ui-data-table-column: A column of the `ui-data-table` it is in. Children, if any, draw each cell, with the row as `row` and its position as `rowIndex`.
  field        string  The row field shown, sorted and filtered, e.g. `amount` or `customer.name`
  label        any  Header text (default: the field)
  sortable     bool  Click the header to sort (default: when it has a `field` or `sortField`)
  sortField    string  Sort by this field instead, e.g. a rank behind a label (default: `field`)
  filter       one of: text, select, range, date  A filter control in the toolbar (`date`: a range calendar with presets)
  options      any  A `select` filter's choices (default: the column's distinct values)
  presets      any  A `date` filter's shortcuts, as `ui-calendar`'s: names such as `lastQuarter`, `yearToDate` or `quarters` (the last four), or `{ label, from, to }`
  fiscalStart  number  A `date` filter's financial year: the month it starts, 1–12; quarters and years follow it
  align        one of: left, center, right  Default: right for numbers, left otherwise
  format       one of: number, currency, percent, date, datetime  How the browser shows the value (in `locale`)
  currency     string  With `format: currency`, e.g. `EUR` (default `USD`)
  decimals     number  Digits after the point for `number`, `currency` and `percent`
  cell         one of: text, badge, progress, sparkline  Draw the value as `badge`, `progress` (0–100) or `sparkline` (needs the chart kit)
  tones        any  With `cell: badge`, a tone per value: `{ Paid: success, Failed: destructive }`
  summary      one of: sum, avg, min, max, count  A footer cell summing (or averaging, …) the rows that pass the filters
  width        any  Column width
  pin          one of: left, right  Keep the column in view while the table scrolls sideways
  tree         bool  The column that shows nesting: indented, with the arrow that opens a row (default: the first)
  hideable     bool  Listed in the View menu (default true)
  hidden       bool  Starts hidden
  group        any  A header over this column and the ones next to it with the same `group`
  groupable    bool  Offered in the View menu's Group by
  resizable    bool  With the table's `resizable`, false keeps this column's width
  edit         one of: text, multiline, number, date, select, checkbox  Its cells can be edited in place; `select` picks from `options` (default: the column's values)
  required     bool  With `edit`: an empty cell is marked wrong
  min          any  With `edit`: the smallest number, or the first date
  max          any  With `edit`: the largest number, or the last date
  pattern      string  With `edit`: a regular expression the whole text must match
  unique       bool  With `edit`: a value used by another row is marked wrong
  message      any  With `edit`: what's said when `min`, `max` or `pattern` isn't met
  id           string  The column's key when it has no field (default: its position)
  children: yes
ui-data-table-toolbar: Controls added to the table's toolbar, after its filters (e.g. an Add or Export button).
  children: yes
ui-data-table-bulk: Actions shown while rows are selected, next to the count. Read the selection from the table's `bindSelection` key.
  children: yes
ui-data-table-detail: A row's details, shown under it when its expander is opened; the row is in scope as `row`.
  children: yes
ui-chart: A chart drawn by Apache ECharts, from rows (`type`, `data`, `x`, `y`) or a full ECharts `option`.
  type         one of: line, area, bar, scatter, effectScatter, pictorialBar, candlestick, boxplot, pie, donut, funnel, radar, heatmap, gauge, tree, treemap, sunburst, sankey, graph, chord, themeRiver, parallel, gantt, pareto  Series type the shorthand builds; leave it out to use `option` alone
  data         any  Rows (objects or arrays), numbers, or a tree / node list, depending on `type`
  x            any  Field (or column) for categories, names or the x value; default the first
  y            any  Field(s) for values: a field, or a list of fields or `{ field, name, …series options }`; default every other numeric field
  value        any  Third field: heatmap cell value, scatter bubble size
  links        any  `{ source, target, value }` for sankey, graph and chord
  option       any  An ECharts option, merged over what the shorthand builds. `{{ }}` works inside it
  filter       any  Keep rows whose fields match: `{ region: "{{ region }}", date: { from, to }, product: [a, b] }`; blank conditions pass
  aggregate    one of: sum, avg, min, max, count  Group rows by `x` (and `series`)
  series       any  Field whose values become separate series (long-format rows)
  sort         any  A field, `-field` for descending, or a list of them; with `series`, orders the categories by their totals
  limit        any  Keep the first N rows after sorting; with `series`, the first N categories; a pareto adds up the rest into one Other bar
  drill        any  Fields to drill through on click, e.g. `[region, country, city]`
  xType        one of: category, time, value, log  The x axis; default: time for dates on lines and points
  zoom         any  Zoom controls along the category or time axis: `inside`, `slider` or `both` (`true`)
  brush        any  Drag to select: `rect` (`true`), `polygon`, `lineX` or `lineY`
  live         any  Live data: `{ url, every, mode: append, window, key, params, paused, stream, pick, into, status }`
  columns      any  Gantt: the table's columns, a field or `{ field, name, width, align }`; the first holds the tree of names (default `[name]`)
  markers      any  Gantt: dated lines down the timeline, `[{ at, name, color }]`
  today        bool  Gantt: a line at today's date when it's on the timeline (default true)
  bindData     statekey  Gantt: the state key `data` reads; bars dragged (or moved with Alt and the arrows) write their new dates back to it
  editable     bool  Gantt: with `bindData`, bars can be moved and stretched, and links drawn and removed (default true)
  visibleRows  number  Gantt: at most this many rows tall; the rest scroll inside the chart, under its dates and beside its table
  workdays     any  Gantt: count and move whole-day tasks on working days, days off shaded: `true` for Monday to Friday, or the weekdays that work (0 is Sunday), e.g. `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4]`
  holidays     any  Gantt: dates that aren't working days either, with `workdays`, e.g. `["2026-12-25"]`
  critical     bool  Gantt: mark the critical path, the tasks with no slack whose delay would move the plan's end (ringed, their links in red)
  baselines    bool  Gantt: draw each task's `baselineStart` and `baselineEnd` (its planned dates) as a thin bar under it, with how late or early it is (default true)
  snap         any  Gantt: the step a task with times of day moves and stretches by, in minutes or as `"15m"`, `"1h"` or `"1d"` (default a day); tasks in whole days move by days
  cascade      any  Gantt: moving or stretching a task moves on the tasks that wait on it, so they start after it ends; `"both"` also pulls them back to start when it ends
  threshold    any  Pareto: a dashed line at this cumulative percent, the bars past it faded (default 80; `false` for none)
  stack        bool  Stack the series
  smooth       bool  Smooth lines
  horizontal   bool  Bars along the x axis
  labels       bool  Show value labels on the marks
  format       one of: number, currency, percent  How values show in labels, tooltips and the value axis, in the document's language
  currency     string  With `format: currency`, e.g. `EUR` (default `USD`)
  decimals     number  Digits after the point in labels and tooltips (default: up to 2)
  legend       bool  Show the legend (default: with two or more series)
  tooltip      bool  Show a tooltip on hover (default true)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 320
  renderer     one of: canvas, svg  Overrides the kit's renderer
  loading      any  Show the loading mask, e.g. `{{ fetching }}`
  bind         statekey  Two-way: the clicked item's name; clicking it again clears it
  bindRow      statekey  The clicked item's row; clicking it again clears it
  bindZoom     statekey  Two-way: the zoom window as `{ from, to }` axis values, or null
  bindLegend   statekey  Two-way: the names of the visible series
  bindBrush    statekey  The rows inside the brushed area
  bindDrill    statekey  Two-way: the drill path, e.g. `[Europe, Germany]`
  maps         any  GeoJSON maps to register first: `{ world: /geo/world.json }`
  group        string  Charts in the same group share tooltips and zoom
  title        any  Accessible name, read before the generated description
  children: no
ui-sparkline: A small chart without axes, for a trend inside text or a stat card.
  data         any (required)  Numbers, or rows with `y`
  y            any  Field holding the value, when `data` has rows
  type         one of: line, area, bar  Default `area`
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 40
  width        any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 100%

  children: no
ui-live-data: Keeps a state key filled from a polled URL, server-sent events or a WebSocket, for any component to read.
  url          any (required)  Polled with GET, or a `ws://` / `wss://` WebSocket; may use state
  into         statekey (required)  State key that holds the data
  every        any  Milliseconds between polls (default 5000, at least 250)
  mode         one of: replace, append  Replace the data with each message (default), or append to it
  window       any  With `append`: keep the last N rows (default 500)
  key          any  With `append`: a row with the same value in this field replaces the old one
  params       any  Query parameters; blank ones are left out, and a change reconnects
  paused       any  Stop while true, e.g. `{{ !liveMode }}`
  stream       bool  Listen to `url` as server-sent events instead of polling
  pick         string  Path to the data in each message, e.g. `data.items`
  status       statekey  State key set to connecting, live, paused or error
  children: no
ui-flow: A diagram of nodes and edges in React Flow's JSON shape. Node and edge types are `ui-flow-node` / `ui-flow-edge` children; `ui-flow-panel` children float above it.
  nodes        any (required)  Nodes as React Flow saves them: `{ id, type, position: { x, y }, data, parentId, width, height, className, style, hidden }`
  edges        any  Edges: `{ id, source, target, sourceHandle, targetHandle, type, label, animated, markerEnd, markerStart, className, style, hidden }`
  layout       any  `layered` places the top-level nodes automatically, ignoring their positions; default: use `position`
  direction    any  `LR` (default), `TB`, `RL` or `BT`: the layout's direction, and where ports without a `side` go
  nodeGap      any  Layout: space between nodes in a rank (default 40)
  rankGap      any  Layout: space between ranks (default 80)
  nodeOrigin   any  Which point of a node `position` names, as fractions: `[0, 0]` top left (default), `[0.5, 0]` top centre
  edgePath     any  Path for edges whose type and template don't name one: `bezier` (default), `straight`, `step` or `smoothstep`
  fit          any  Fit the view to the nodes when they first appear (default true)
  fitPadding   any  Space left around the nodes when fitting, as a fraction of the view (default 0.1)
  viewport     any  The view to start at when `fit` is false: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  center       any  A node id: the view pans to that node whenever this changes
  highlight    any  `neighbors`: while a node is selected, dim everything not connected to it
  selectable   any  Click or Enter selects a node or edge; Shift adds to the selection (default true)
  editable     any  Turns on `draggable`, `connectable` and `deletable` together (default false)
  draggable    any  Nodes can be dragged (default: `editable`)
  connectable  any  Drag from a port to another to connect them; needs `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  deletable    any  Delete or Backspace removes the selection; needs `bindNodes` / `bindEdges` (default: `editable`)
  connect      any  Connection rules: `{ sameParent, self, unique, pairs: [{ source, target }] }` (node types)
  newEdge      any  Fields every new edge starts with, e.g. `{ type: smoothstep, markerEnd: arrowclosed }`
  newNode      any  A node (`{ type, data }`) made where a connection is dropped on empty canvas, and joined to it
  confirmDelete any  The id of a dialog to open before deleting; its button sends `flow.delete`
  pan          any  Drag the background to pan (default true)
  zoom         any  Wheel, pinch and keys zoom (default true)
  wheel        any  What the wheel does: `zoom` (default) or `pan` (Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms)
  minZoom      any  Default 0.1
  maxZoom      any  Default 2
  background   one of: dots, lines, none  Background pattern (default dots)
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  minimap      bool  An overview in the corner that pans the view (default false)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 480. The width is the container's
  title        any  Accessible name
  bind         statekey  State key holding the selected node's id (null when none)
  bindNodes    statekey  State key that gets the nodes, with new positions, after a drag
  bindViewport statekey  State key kept in sync with the view: `{ x, y, zoom }`
  nodeStyles   any  Apply each node's saved `style` and `className` (default true). Turn off when the template works the look out from `data`
  filter       any  Node ids to show; the rest are hidden, except the nodes they connect to, shown as context (`data-neighbor`). Empty or null shows all
  filterNeighbors any  With `filter`, also show the nodes the shown ones connect to (default true)
  search       any  Text to find in the nodes: matches are marked `data-match`, everything else is dimmed
  bindMatches  statekey  State key holding the ids of the nodes `search` matches
  bindHistory  statekey  State key holding how many edits can be undone and redone: `{ undo, redo }`
  bindEdges    statekey  State key that gets the edges after a connection or a deletion
  bindNode     statekey  State key holding the selected node itself (its `id`, `type`, `data`, …), or null: for a side panel that shows or edits it
  bindSelection statekey  State key holding every selected node and edge: `{ nodes: [ids], edges: [ids] }`
  bindDelete   statekey  With `confirmDelete`: what would be deleted, `{ nodes, edges }`, while the dialog is open
  parts: controls, minimap
  children: yes
ui-flow-node: A node type of the `ui-flow` it is in: its children are drawn for every node of that `type`, with the node in scope as `node`. Place `ui-flow-port`s inside.
  type         string  The node type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  variant      one of: card, plain  `card` (default) gives the node a border, background and padding; `plain` leaves all of it to `style`
  shape        any  The node's outline: `rect`, `rounded`, `pill`, `circle`, `ellipse`, `diamond`, `hexagon`, `parallelogram`, `triangle` or `cylinder`; or `polygon` with `points`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ node.data.shape }}`. Style it through `parts.shape` (`fill`, `stroke`)
  points       any  With `shape: polygon`: the corners as percentages of the box, e.g. `50,0 100,50 50,100 0,50`
  container    bool  Other nodes can sit inside it: dragging a node onto it makes it the node's parent, and off it, takes it out
  resizable    bool  A handle in the bottom-right corner resizes the node; the size is saved as its `width` and `height`
  minWidth     number  Smallest width when resizing (default 80)
  minHeight    number  Smallest height when resizing (default 40)
  parts: shape
  children: yes
ui-flow-edge: An edge type of the `ui-flow` it is in. Its `style` styles the path (`stroke`, `stroke-width`, …); its children, with the edge in scope as `edge`, are the label. Without children the label is `edge.label`.
  type         string  The edge type this template draws. Leave it out (or use `default`) for every type no other template declares
  path         one of: bezier, straight, step, smoothstep  Path shape; default: the edge's own type when it is one of these, else the flow's `edgePath`
  marker       one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the target, unless the edge has `markerEnd`
  markerStart  one of: none, arrow, arrowclosed  Arrowhead at the source, unless the edge has `markerStart`
  animated     bool  Moving dashes, unless the edge sets `animated`
  floating     bool  Attach to the nodes' borders, facing each other, instead of to ports
  parts: label
  children: yes
ui-flow-port: Where edges attach to a node, in a `ui-flow-node`. It is placed on its side of the nearest positioned element: the node, or e.g. a table row with `position: relative`.
  id           any  The port's id, matched against an edge's `sourceHandle` / `targetHandle`. May use the node, e.g. `{{ c.handle }}`
  type         one of: source, target  Edges leave from `source` ports (default) and arrive at `target` ports
  side         any  `left`, `right`, `top` or `bottom`. Default: from the flow's `direction`, e.g. targets left and sources right for `LR`
  offset       any  Where along the side, e.g. `30%` or `24px`. Default: ports on one side share it evenly
  accepts      any  Node types allowed at the other end of a new connection, e.g. `[step, merge]`
  max          any  How many edges this port takes at most
  scope        one of: children  `children`: connects only to nodes inside this node (a container), whatever `sameParent` says
  connectable  any  Whether new connections can start or end here (default true)
  children: no
ui-flow-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-flow`, e.g. a toolbar. It doesn't pan or zoom.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the flow (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-flow-item: A palette entry: drag it onto a `ui-flow` to add its `node` there, or click it to add the node in the middle of the view. The flow needs `bindNodes`.
  node         any (required)  The node to add: `{ type, data }`, and `id` if it should keep one
  flow         string  The element id of the flow to add to. Default: the flow it is in, or the page's only flow
  children: yes
ui-map: A map, on OpenStreetMap or Google Maps, with markers, popups, shapes, clusters and picking a place. A `ui-map-popup` child is the popup's content; `ui-map-panel` children float above it.
  provider     one of: osm, google  `osm` (default): OpenStreetMap, no key needed. `google`: Google Maps, which needs an API key
  markers      any  Places, as rows: `{ id, lat, lng, title, description, label, tone, color, alarm, effect, href, draggable }`, usually from data or state. `label` is a letter, number or emoji in the pin
  latField     string  The rows' latitude field (default `lat`, else `latitude`)
  lngField     string  The rows' longitude field (default `lng`, else `lon`, `long` or `longitude`)
  titleField   string  The rows' title field (default `title`, else `name`)
  toneBy       any  Colours markers by a field: `{ field: status, tones: { late: danger, done: success } }`
  alarmBy      any  Which markers are in alarm: `{ field: status, values: [offline, fault] }`, or `alarm: true` on a row. They pulse in red with a `!`, stay on top, and a new one is announced
  effectBy     any  Animates markers by a field: `{ field: status, effects: { late: glow } }`, or `effect` on a row: `pulse`, `glow`, `bounce` or `blink`. Still, where the viewer asked for less motion
  filter       any  Shows only the markers that pass: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-data-table`'s and `ui-chart`'s `filter`, e.g. a `ui-filters` panel's `bind`
  shapes       any  Lines, areas and circles: `{ id, type: line | area | circle, points: [[lat, lng], …], center, radius (metres), title, tone, color, width, dashed, fill }`
  geojson      any  GeoJSON lines and areas, styled by each feature's `properties` (`tone`, `color`, `width`, `title`); its points become markers
  overlays     any  Layers over the map: `{ id, type: image, url, bounds: [[south, west], [north, east]] }`, e.g. a floor plan; `{ type: tiles, url, attribution }`, e.g. sea marks; `{ type: heat, points, weightField, radius, max }`. Each with `opacity` and `show`, which may use state
  center       any  `[lat, lng]` or `{ lat, lng }`. The map moves when it changes. Default: fitted to what's on it
  zoom         any  0 (the world) to 19 (a building); default 13 with a `center`
  minZoom      number  How far out it zooms
  maxZoom      number  How far in it zooms, and the closest it fits to
  fit          any  Fits the view to the markers and shapes when it opens (default: without a `center`); `always`: whenever they change
  cluster      any  Groups markers closer than this many px (`true`: 56), with how many there are; clicking a group zooms to it
  bind         statekey  State key with the selected marker's id (null when none). Setting it selects that marker and brings it into view
  bindMarker   statekey  State key with the selected marker itself, or null
  bindShape    statekey  State key with the id of the shape last clicked; shapes are clickable with it
  bindView     statekey  State key kept at `{ center, zoom, bounds: { north, south, east, west } }`
  bindVisible  statekey  State key with the ids of the markers in view, e.g. for a list beside the map
  bindAlarms   statekey  State key with the ids of the markers in alarm, e.g. for a count
  bindPoint    statekey  Picks a place: clicking the map puts a pin there, which can be dragged, and writes `{ lat, lng }`
  bindMarkers  statekey  State key the rows are in: a dragged marker's new place is written back to its row
  bindLocation statekey  State key that gets `{ lat, lng, accuracy }` after My location
  draggable    any  Markers can be dragged, or moved with Alt and the arrow keys (needs `bindMarkers`)
  popup        bool  Opens a popup over the selected marker, with its title and description or the `ui-map-popup` (default true)
  locate       bool  A My location button: shows where the viewer is, once they allow it
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  gestures     one of: cooperative, greedy, none  `cooperative` (default): the page scrolls past the map, and Ctrl / ⌘ + wheel or two fingers zoom it. `greedy`: the map takes the wheel and one finger. `none`: it stays put
  tiles        any  With `osm`, another tile server: `{ url, attribution, attributionUrl, maxZoom, darkUrl }`, `url` having `{z}`, `{x}` and `{y}`
  darkTiles    bool  With `osm`, darken the tiles in dark mode when there's no `darkUrl` (default true)
  apiKey       any  With `google`, the API key (default: the one the host set). Browsers see it, so restrict it to your sites
  mapId        any  With `google`, a map id from Google's console, for its cloud styles
  mapType      one of: roadmap, satellite, hybrid, terrain  With `google` (default `roadmap`)
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 400. The width is the container's
  title        any  Names the map for screen readers (default `Map`)
  parts: controls
  children: yes
ui-map-popup: What a `ui-map`'s popup shows, with the selected marker in scope as `marker`.
  children: yes
ui-map-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-map`, e.g. a legend or a search box. It doesn't move with the map.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the map (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-twin: A digital twin: a 3D world drawn with three.js from models of most formats, every part of it configurable and able to use state, with machine and sensor values shown on the objects, alarms, paths things follow, zones, views and editing the layout. A `ui-twin-popup` child is the popup's content; `ui-twin-panel` children float above it.
  models       any  The models by name: `{ forklift: models/forklift.glb, pump: { url, scale, units: m | cm | mm | in | ft, up: y | z, rotate, fit, origin: base | center | none, format, mtl, color } }`. glTF / GLB (with Draco, meshopt and KTX2), OBJ (with `mtl`), FBX, STL, PLY, DAE, 3MF, 3DS, WRL and USD / USDZ. `fit`: the largest side in metres, or `[w, h, d]` to fit in. Each is made to stand on the ground at its middle unless `origin` says otherwise. `far`: how it's drawn far from the camera, a simpler model's url, `{ url, distance }`, `{ ratio, distance }` (made simpler in the browser, `ratio` of its triangles) or `false` (see `lod`)
  objects      any  What's in the world, as rows: `{ id, model | shape: box | cylinder | sphere | cone | sensor | point, size, color, position: [x, z] | [x, y, z], rotation (degrees, or [x, y, z]), scale, title, description, label, tone, alarm, effect, path, speed, progress, loop, face, attach, animation, opacity, clickable, href, … }`, in metres with y up. Any other fields are the object's data (a machine's speed, a sensor's value): `readouts` show them. Usually from data or state, so they move when it changes
  readouts     any  Values shown on the objects that have them: `[{ field, label, unit, decimals, warn, alarm, below, tag, when, models, history }]`. Past `warn` an object turns warning, past `alarm` it's in alarm (`below: true`: under them); `when` (a `filter`) or `models` limit a readout to some objects, so each kind can have its own limits. The first two are on its tag (`tag` says otherwise); all are in its popup. `history: n` keeps an object's last n values (a point each time it changes, up to 500) and draws them as a sparkline in its popup
  colorBy      any  Colours objects by a value: `{ field, min, max, colors: [blue, green, yellow, red] }`, e.g. temperatures
  live         any  Machine and sensor values from a feed of the twin's own: `{ url, every: 5000 }` polled, or `{ stream: url }` (server-sent events). Each answer is rows with an `id`, or `{ <id>: { field: value } }`, merged into the objects with that id
  paths        any  Routes: `{ id, points: [[x, z], …], closed, width, tone, color, flow, height, show }`. `flow: true` (or a speed) moves stripes along it; an object with `path` follows it at `speed` m/s (default 1), or stands at `progress` (0 to 1)
  zones        any  Areas on the ground: `{ id, points: [[x, z], …] | center: [x, z] and size: [w, d], tone, color, label, title, description, height, opacity }`. With `bindZone` or a `title` they can be clicked
  walls        any  Walls: `{ points: [[x, z], …], closed, height (default 3), thickness (default 0.2), color, opacity }`
  ground       any  `{ size: [w, d], center, color, grid: 1 (metres a cell) | false }`, or false for none. Default: big enough for everything, with a 1 m grid
  environment  any  `{ preset: studio | day | night, light (default 1), shadows (default true), background, fog }`
  camera       any  `{ position: [x, y, z], target: [x, y, z], fov }`. The camera moves there when it changes. Default: fitted to the world
  views        any  Named views, shown as buttons: `[{ id, label, position, target }]`
  world        any  All of the above in one object (`{ models, objects, paths, zones, walls, ground, environment, camera, views, readouts, colorBy }`), e.g. a layout kept in state; a prop of its own wins
  src          any  The address of such a world as JSON, fetched in the browser
  follow       any  The id of an object the camera follows, keeping its distance
  filter       any  Shows only the objects that pass: `{ field: condition }`, as `ui-data-table`'s and `ui-chart`'s `filter`, e.g. a `ui-filters` panel's `bind`
  toneBy       any  Tones objects by a field: `{ field: status, tones: { running: success, idle: neutral, fault: danger } }`; a ring in it is drawn under each
  alarmBy      any  Which objects are in alarm: `{ field: status, values: [fault] }`, or `alarm: true` on a row, or a readout past `alarm`. They glow red, get a `!` tag, and a new one is announced
  effectBy     any  Animates objects by a field: `{ field: state, effects: { running: spin } }`, or `effect` on a row: `pulse`, `glow`, `blink`, `spin` (`spin`: degrees a second) or `bob`. Still, where the viewer asked for less motion
  labels       one of: auto, all, none  Tags over objects: `auto` (default) for those with a `label`, readouts or an alarm; `all`; `none` (alarms still)
  editable     any  Objects can be dragged on the ground, or moved with Alt and the arrow keys and turned with Alt+R (needs `bindObjects`)
  multiple     bool  Several objects picked at once: ⌘, Ctrl or Shift and a click adds or takes one away (on the view, a tag or the list), Shift and a drag from the floor draws a box around more, ⌘A picks them all. Editable, they're dragged, moved, turned and removed together. The last one picked is the selected one (`bind`); all are in `bindSelected`
  snap         any  Metres moves snap to, e.g. 0.5
  measure      any  A ruler button among the controls (or M with the view focused): two clicks, on objects, walls or the floor, and the distance between them is drawn and said, with how far across and how far up when both count. Picked from a tag or the list, an object counts from its middle on the floor. Escape stops
  palette      any  While `editable`, things to add, as rows like `objects` without a place: `[{ label, model | shape, title, … }]`. Clicked, one is added in the middle of the view; dragged into it, where it's dropped. Delete removes the selected object
  bind         statekey  State key with the selected object's id (null when none). Setting it selects that object and brings it into view
  bindObject   statekey  State key with the selected object itself, with its latest values
  bindSelected statekey  State key with the ids of the objects picked (with `multiple`, several; else the selected one's); setting it picks them
  bindZone     statekey  State key with the id of the zone last clicked
  bindView     statekey  State key with the current view's id; setting it moves the camera there
  bindAlarms   statekey  State key with the ids of the objects in alarm, e.g. for a count
  bindObjects  statekey  State key the objects are in: a moved one's `position` and `rotation` are written back to its row
  bindLive     statekey  State key that gets the latest values from `live`, as `{ <id>: { field: value } }`, e.g. for a list or totals beside the twin
  bindMeasure  statekey  State key with the last measurement, `{ from, to, distance, across, up }` in metres (null when none)
  bindCamera   statekey  State key kept at `{ position, target }` after the camera's moved, e.g. to copy into `views`
  popup        bool  Opens a popup over the selected object, with its title, description and readouts or the `ui-twin-popup` (default true)
  controls     bool  Zoom and fit buttons (default true)
  gestures     one of: orbit, none  `orbit` (default): drag to turn, right-drag or two fingers to move, wheel or pinch to zoom. `none`: the camera stays put
  transition   number  Milliseconds an object takes to move to a new place from the data (default 600; 0 jumps)
  quality      one of: high, low  `low`: no shadows or smoothing, for big worlds or slow devices
  lod          any  Models drawn simpler far from the camera: `auto` (default) for a model used by 100 objects or more, `true` for every model, `false` (or `none`) for none, or `{ ratio, distance }` (default 0.15 of the triangles, past twelve times the model's size and at least 15 m) for every model. Made in the browser with meshoptimizer's simplifier; a model's own `far` wins. Only for objects drawn together (not those in a look of their own)
  motionScale  number  While the camera moves, the view is drawn at this share of its resolution each way (default 0.65), and sharp again 400 ms after it stops; 1 keeps it sharp
  height       any  Number (px) or CSS length; default 480. The width is the container's
  title        any  Names the view for screen readers (default `3D view`)
  parts: controls
  children: yes
ui-twin-popup: What a `ui-twin`'s popup shows, with the selected object (and its latest values) in scope as `object`.
  children: yes
ui-twin-panel: Content that floats above a `ui-twin`, e.g. a legend, counts or filters. It doesn't move with the camera.
  position     one of: top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right  Corner or edge of the view (default top-left)
  children: yes
ui-icon: An SVG icon from the icon kit's packs, drawn in the current text colour.
  name         string (required)  `pack:icon` (e.g. `logistics:truck`) or a bare `icon`, found in the first pack that has it
  variant      one of: outline, filled  `outline` (default) or `filled`
  size         any  Number (px) or CSS length; default `1em`, the size of the text around it, times the theme's `size.icon`
  label        any  Accessible name. Without one the icon is decorative and hidden from screen readers
  children: no
```


---


# iRender

[![CI](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Build UI from configuration. Write a document in JSON or YAML, then validate it and render it to HTML with a ~4.5 KB (gzipped) runtime for state and actions.

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/blocks/pricing.yaml --ui-kit --icon-kit -o pricing.html
cargo run -p irender-cli -- validate skills/irender/examples/counter.yaml
cargo run -p irender-cli -- components   # built-in components and their props
cargo run -p irender-cli -- schema       # JSON Schema for documents
```

See [`examples/`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/examples/README.md) for complete pages: galleries for the kits, blocks (dashboards, data tables, sign-in, chat and more), and flows (ER diagrams, process canvases and workflows). To browse them all, run `examples/build.sh`, then `python3 examples/serve.py` (a static server plus the live endpoints the chart gallery uses).

## Writing documents with an LLM

- **[`llms.txt`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/llms.txt)** is an index of the docs for models, and [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/llms-full.txt) puts all of them in one file to paste into a context window.
- **[`skills/irender`](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/skills/irender/SKILL.md)** is an [Agent Skill](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview) that writes, validates and renders documents. It's linked into `.claude/skills` here. To use it in another project, copy the folder into that project's `.claude/skills/` or into `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **The validation loop:** both tell the model to check its output with `irender validate`, which reports every problem at its path, so it can fix them all before rendering. For documents a model writes for end users, validate and render with `--untrusted`.
- **Regenerating:** `tools/llm-docs.sh` regenerates the component and icon references, the copies of the READMEs and examples, and `llms-full.txt` from the CLI and the sources. `tools/llm-docs.sh --check` fails when they're stale. The hand-written sources are `llms.txt`, `skills/irender/SKILL.md`, `skills/irender/references/authoring.md` and the skill's `counter.yaml` and `wizard.yaml`.

## Crates

| crate | role |
|---|---|
| `irender-core` | Document model (serde), expressions, theme tokens, policy, validation → IR. No HTML. |
| `irender-style` | Compiles style blocks into hashed, deduplicated classes in cascade layers; CSS validation and minification via lightningcss. |
| `irender-html` | Server-side renderer, component registry, built-ins, browser runtime. No web-framework dependency. |
| `irender-cli` | `validate`, `render` (with `--timings`, `--repeat`, `--parallel`, `--minify`, `--ui-kit`, `--chart-kit`, `--flow-kit`, `--map-kit`, `--twin-kit`, `--icon-kit`, `--icons`), `app` (a manifest, icons and a service worker), `schema`, `components`, `icons`. |
| `irender-ui-kit` | Optional, shadcn-style components (`ui-button`, `ui-card`, `ui-alert`, form controls, table, pagination, a sidebar layout, …) and a matching theme. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-chart-kit` | Optional charts drawn by Apache ECharts: `ui-chart` (shorthand for 23 series types including a Gantt chart, or any ECharts option), `ui-sparkline` and `ui-live-data`: filters, grouping and drill-downs in the browser, clicks, zoom, legend and brush as state, live polling, SSE and WebSocket data, themed from the document's tokens. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-icon-kit` | Optional `ui-icon`: original SVG icons, outline and filled, in packs (core, arrows, status, logistics, warehouse, retail, manufacturing, accounting, agriculture, automotive, aviation, banking, construction, education, energy, finance, healthcare, hospitality, hr, insurance, it, legal, marketing, maritime, media, mining, oil-gas, public-sector, robotics, simulation, social, space, sports, telecom) drawn to one standard, a `brands` pack of social and sign-in logo marks, plus your own packs from SVG files, sanitized on load. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-icon-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-flow-kit` | Optional `ui-flow`: node-and-edge diagrams from React Flow's JSON, with node and edge types written as ordinary iRender trees, ports from node data, layered layout, pan and zoom, selection, dragging, connecting with rules, deleting with confirmation, a palette, containers, copy and paste, undo, search and a minimap. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-flow-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-map-kit` | Optional `ui-map`: maps on OpenStreetMap (no key) or Google Maps, with markers, popups of any components, clusters, shapes and GeoJSON, picking a place, dragging markers, and the selection, view and what's in it as state. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-map-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-twin-kit` | Optional `ui-twin`: digital twins, 3D worlds drawn with three.js from glTF, OBJ, FBX, STL, USD and other models, every part of them configuration, with machine and sensor values on the objects, limits and alarms, colours by value, paths, live feeds and editing a layout. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-twin-kit/README.md). |
| `irender-wasm` | The renderer for the browser: renders a chat message's UI JSON in the page, for replies that arrive without server-rendered markup. Not published. See its [README](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-wasm/README.md). |

## A node

```json
{
  "type": "button",
  "props": { "label": "{{ qty == 1 ? 'Buy now' : 'Buy ' + qty }}", "disabled": "{{ qty < 1 }}" },
  "attrs": { "id": "buy", "aria-label": "Buy", "data-sku": "{{ product.sku }}" },
  "class": ["cta"],
  "style": {
    "padding": "12px 20px",
    "background": "$color.primary",
    "width": "{{ qty * 10 }}%",
    ":hover": { "transform": "translateY(-1px)" },
    "@md": { "padding": 16 },
    "@dark": { "box-shadow": "none" }
  },
  "parts": { "label": { "style": { "font-weight": 600 } } },
  "on": { "click": { "action": "set_state", "key": "qty", "value": "{{ qty + 1 }}" } }
}
```

- **props** are typed per component and validated.
- **attrs** accept any HTML attribute and override the component's defaults.
- **style** accepts any CSS property, including nested `:pseudo`, `&selector`, `@breakpoint`, `@variant` and `@media …` blocks. Numbers get `px` where it makes sense, and `$tokens` compile to `var(--…)`.
- **parts** style a component's inner elements.
- **on** maps DOM events to declarative actions: `set_state`, `navigate`, `submit`, `call` and `wait`. A `call` dispatches an `irender:call` DOM event for the host app to handle. A `wait` (`{ "action": "wait", "ms": 3000 }`, at most 60 000) pauses before the next action, e.g. to hide a message again.
- **Expressions** (`{{ … }}`) support paths, literals, arithmetic, comparisons, `&& || !`, `?:` and the functions `range`, `includes`, `toggle` and `round`. An expression that references `state` updates live in the browser. Any other path is filled in from server `data` at render time.
  - Paths: `user.name`, `rows[0].id`, `obj['first-name']`, and computed keys, such as `names[dim]` (the field `dim` names) or `rows[i + 1]`. A key that's neither a string nor a whole number from 0 gives `null`.
  - `range(n)` is the list `[0, 1, …, n - 1]`, and `range(start, end)` runs from `start` to `end - 1`, for a `list` that repeats something a number of times: `"items": "{{ range(stars) }}"`.
  - Arguments are truncated to whole numbers, and anything that isn't a number counts as 0.
  - At most 1000 items.
  - `includes(list, value)` says whether the list has the value (compared as `==`), and `toggle(list, value)` is the list without it if it has it, or with it added at the end. Together they keep a set of choices in state: a button whose `aria-pressed` is `"{{ includes(tags, 'rust') }}"` and whose click sets `tags` to `"{{ toggle(tags, 'rust') }}"`. Anything not a list counts as empty.
  - `round(x)` rounds to a whole number and `round(x, digits)` to that many decimals (0 to 10), halves away from zero: `{{ round(oee, 1) }}`. Anything not a number counts as 0.
  - These are the only functions. `.field` and `[i]` follow paths only, so `range(n).length` isn't allowed.
  - In `style`, a value from an expression is set on the element itself: `null` (or a value that's dropped as unsafe) leaves the property as if it weren't declared, never taking a parent's value, and `inherit`, `initial`, `unset` and `revert` work. Under `:hover`, a media query or a nested selector those keywords count as no value.
- **Built-in components:** `element`, `text`, `stack`, `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `list` and `if`. Run `irender components` for their props. `include` and `else` are handled by the resolver; see below.
- **Cascade order:** theme variables → `i-base` layer (component defaults) → `i-instance` layer (the document's `style`). The document always wins.

### Theme

A document's `theme` sets design tokens (`$color.primary` in styles is `var(--color-primary)`), `modes` that override them under a variant (`dark`), `breakpoints` and `variants`. `options` are sets of overrides people choose between on the page: a palette, a corner radius, a density.

```yaml
theme:
  tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } }
  options:
    palette:
      label: Colour
      default: indigo
      choices:
        indigo: { tokens: { color: { primary: "#4f46e5" } } }
        rose:
          label: Rose
          tokens: { color: { primary: "#e11d48" } }
          modes: { dark: { color: { primary: "#fb7185" } } }
```

- A choice applies through `data-theme-<option>` on `<html>` (`data-theme-palette="rose"`); its `modes` give its own values under a variant, so a palette has its own dark colours. A token a choice sets without a dark value keeps it in dark mode.
- The default choice (`default`, or the first) is part of the base tokens: a page with nothing chosen looks like it.
- A choice also applies to part of a page: `attrs: { data-theme-density: compact }` on a node makes everything inside it compact, and `data-theme-palette: zinc` there undoes a palette picked for the page. Each choice sets every token its option touches, and tokens computed from them again, so this works for the default choice too.
- The built-in `space.*` and `font.size.*` tokens follow `space.scale` and `font.scale` (`$space.md` is `calc(16px * var(--space-scale, 1))`), so a density or text-size option reaches styles that use them. Finer factors on top: `space.inset` (paddings), `space.gap` (gaps and margins), `size.control` (control heights) and `size.icon` (icons), all 1 by default; the built-in `button` and `input` paddings and a `stack`'s `gap` in px follow them. The built-in `button` and `input` also follow `border.width`, `radius.control` and `font.weight.medium` when a theme sets them (irender-ui-kit's options do).
- Option and choice names use lowercase letters, digits and `-`. Mistakes are reported with their paths, like other theme errors.
- [irender-ui-kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-ui-kit/README.md#theme-options) ships options (palette, radius, density, text size, font) and `ui-theme-option`, which picks one, remembers it and applies it before the page shows. The [chart kit](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/crates/irender-chart-kit/README.md#theme) adds chart colour schemes. A document adds choices to these or options of its own.

### Language and interface text

`lang` is the document's language: the page's `<html lang>`, and the plural rules for its labels. `labels` gives the kits' fixed words (buttons, counts, empty and loading messages, what screen readers hear) in that language, keyed by the English. Keys a document doesn't give stay English.

```yaml
version: 1
lang: es
labels:
  "Rows per page": "Filas por página"
  "Page {page} of {pages}": "Página {page} de {pages}"
  "{n} results": { one: "{n} resultado", other: "{n} resultados" }
root: …
```

- `{name}` marks a value filled in; keep it in your text, anywhere in it.
- A count's key (one with `{n}`) takes plural forms, `{ one, other }`, plus `zero`, `two`, `few` or `many` where the language has them. The browser picks with `Intl.PluralRules` for `lang`, and the server follows the same rules for the common languages (English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, German, Italian, Dutch, Polish, Russian, Ukrainian, Czech, Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Japanese, Chinese, Korean and others; the rest as English). A single text is used for every count. The count is written in the language's way (`1.234` in German), on the server and in the browser alike.
- Every key, by kit and component, is in [the labels reference](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/skills/irender/references/labels.md), generated from the source by `tools/labels.py`.
- Dates and numbers aren't labels: they follow each component's `locale`, which defaults to `lang` (and without either, to the browser's).
- **Right to left.** A language written right to left (Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu, …) gives the page `dir="rtl"`: the kits' layouts mirror (sidebars, menus, tables, calendars, the order of things in a row), icons that point along the line turn round, and Left and Right swap in the keyboard and in dragging. Charts and flow diagrams keep their left-to-right geometry, and codes, shortcuts and counts such as `2 / 3` read left to right.
- A component reads a label with `cx.label("…")`, `cx.label_with("…", &[(name, value)])` or `cx.label_count(one, other, n)` on the server, and `window.__irender.label(text, vars)` in the browser (`[one, other]` for a count).

### Apps

`app` makes a document's pages an installable app:

```yaml
app:
  name: Field inspections
  shortName: Inspect
  themeColor: "#ffffff"
  themeColorDark: "#09090b"
  icon: { text: FI, background: "#1d4ed8" }     # or icons: [{ src, sizes, type, purpose }]
  shortcuts: [ { name: New, url: "./?new" } ]
  share: { url: "./new.html", accept: ["image/*"] }
  files: [ { url: "./", accept: { text/csv: [.csv] } } ]
  offline: { skip: [/api/], fallback: offline.html }
```

```sh
irender render app.yaml --ui-kit -o site/index.html
irender app app.yaml --dir site
```

- Each rendered page links the manifest, its colours and icons, and registers the service worker. `base` is where those are from the page (default `./`).
- `irender app` writes `manifest.webmanifest`, the icons (when they're made from letters) and `sw.js` into the folder of rendered pages. Run it last, each time they change: the service worker's version comes from what's in the folder.
- The service worker keeps the pages and files with the endings in `offline.files`, up to `offline.maxKb` each, and the libraries the pages load from jsDelivr (and `offline.also`). Pages come from the network when it answers in time, else from what's kept. Paths in `offline.skip` always go to the network.
- It's one app a folder, served over https (or localhost). An untrusted document can't be one.

## Form controls

`input`, `select` and `textarea` take `bind: <state key>` to keep a state value in sync both ways.

```json
{ "type": "select", "props": { "bind": "country", "placeholder": "Country",
  "options": [{ "value": "in", "label": "India" }, { "value": "de", "label": "Germany", "disabled": true }] } }
{ "type": "input", "props": { "type": "radio", "bind": "size", "value": "m" } }
{ "type": "input", "props": { "type": "checkbox", "bind": "gift" } }
{ "type": "textarea", "props": { "bind": "notes", "rows": 4 } }
```

- **`select`:** `options` is an array of plain values or `{ value, label, disabled }`. If it comes from server data, the options are fixed. If it reads `state`, the browser rebuilds them when the array changes and keeps the current choice. `placeholder` adds a first, empty option that shows while the key is empty. `multiple: true` makes it a list box where several can be picked (Ctrl or ⌘ and a click, Shift for a run); the key holds a list, of numbers when it held numbers, and has no placeholder.
- **Radios:** a bound radio needs a `value`. It is checked when the state equals that value, and choosing it writes the value. Radios bound to the same key share `name` automatically, so the browser keeps one checked.
- **Checkboxes:** a bound checkbox stores `true` / `false`.
- **Types:** the DOM holds option and radio values as text. If a key starts out as a number, choosing a radio or option keeps it a number, as a `number` input does. Otherwise it becomes a string.

## Dynamic content

Parts of a page can come from API calls or other runtime work in four ways. Pick by *when* the data is known.

| known when | use |
|---|---|
| the request comes in | server `data`: `engine.render(&ir, &data)`. `{{ path }}`, `list` and `if` read it. The document is loaded once and reused. |
| the document is loaded | `include` fragments built by your code (below), or build the whole `Document` in code and call `engine.resolve(&doc)`. |
| after the page loads, in the browser | `submit` with `into` stores a JSON response in `state`. Text, attributes, `if` and `list` that use that key update. |
| the page opens | `on: { mount: … }` runs actions as soon as an element appears. |

### `if`

```json
{ "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ user.admin }}" }, "children": [ … ] }
```

It renders its children only when `when` is truthy, and adds no element of its own. A condition that only reads server `data` is decided on the server and leaves nothing behind. A condition that reads `state` puts the content between two empty `<template>` markers, and the runtime moves it in and out of the page as the condition changes. The markers are valid anywhere, including inside `<table>` and `<ul>`. Hidden content keeps its DOM nodes, so input values and listeners survive being hidden. Note that the markers count as siblings for `:first-child` / `:nth-child`.

An `else` right after an `if` renders its children when the `if` doesn't. Give it a `when` to make it an else-if, and chain as many as you like; a plain `else` ends the chain:

```json
{ "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ n > 2 }}" }, "children": [ … ] },
{ "type": "else", "props": { "when": "{{ n > 0 }}" }, "children": [ … ] },
{ "type": "else", "children": [ … ] }
```

The resolver turns each `else` into an `if` whose condition is that no earlier branch matched, so it behaves exactly like one, including updating live when a condition reads `state`. An `else` takes only `when` and children, and must directly follow an `if` or an `else` with `when`.

### Lists that change in the browser

When `items` reads `state`, `list` also writes its children once into a `<template>` as its first child. When the array changes, the runtime rebuilds every item from that template. The server still renders the initial items, so the page is complete without JavaScript.

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "state": { "results": [], "loading": false },
  "root": { "type": "stack", "children": [
    { "type": "element",
      "on": { "mount": [
        { "action": "set_state", "key": "loading", "value": true },
        { "action": "submit", "method": "GET", "endpoint": "/api/search", "into": "results" },
        { "action": "set_state", "key": "loading", "value": false } ] } },
    { "type": "if", "props": { "when": "{{ loading }}" },
      "children": [{ "type": "text", "props": { "value": "Loading…" } }] },
    { "type": "list", "props": { "items": "{{ results }}", "as": "r", "tag": "ul" },
      "children": [{ "type": "text", "props": { "tag": "li", "value": "{{ r.title }}" },
                     "on": { "click": { "action": "call", "name": "open", "args": { "id": "{{ r.id }}" } } } }] } ] } }
```

Inside a rebuilt item, `item` and `index` (or your `as` / `index` names) are known only in the browser. They work in everything that updates live: text, attributes, classes, `{{ }}` style values, `if`, nested `list` and action arguments. Props that a component reads once on the server, such as `tag`, `variant` or `type`, cannot depend on them. Actions in a list run one after another, and `submit` waits for its response, so `loading` flags work as shown above.

Without a `key`, every item is rebuilt when the array changes, so focus and typed input inside an item are lost. Give `list` a `key` (e.g. `"key": "{{ r.id }}"`) and an item whose key is still in the new array keeps its DOM nodes: input values, focus and hidden `if` content survive, `mount` doesn't run again, and only text and attributes that read the item or `index` update. Items are moved only when they're out of order. Keys should be unique; a repeated key reuses one old item per occurrence. A keyed list's server-rendered items are replaced by template items when the page starts, because the server baked their values into plain HTML.

### `mount` actions

`on: { mount: … }` runs when the element first appears: at page start, or when an `if` shows it or a list rebuilds it. A server-rendered element mounts once. The name doesn't clash with `<img>`'s native `load` event, which still works through `on: { load: … }`.

### `include`

```json
{ "version": 1,
  "fragments": { "card": { "type": "stack", "children": [ { "type": "text", "props": { "value": "{{ item.name }}" } } ] } },
  "root": { "type": "list", "props": { "items": "{{ products }}" },
            "children": [{ "type": "include", "props": { "name": "card" } }] } }
```

An `include` node is replaced by its fragment when the document is loaded. The fragment is validated like the rest of the document, with paths such as `root.children[0]@card.props.value`, and it sees the scope it's included in. Fragments are looked up in the document's `fragments` first, then in `engine.fragments`:

```rust
use irender_core::{FragmentDir, NodeSpec};

engine.fragments = Some(Arc::new(FragmentDir("ui/fragments".into())));   // <name>.json / .yaml; CLI: --fragments DIR
// or build them from anything known at load time:
engine.fragments = Some(Arc::new(move |name: &str| -> Result<Option<NodeSpec>, String> {
    match name {
        "promo" => Ok(Some(serde_json::from_value(fetch_promo_config()?).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?)),
        _ => Ok(None),
    }
}));
```

`include` takes `props.name`, which must be a fixed name, and optionally `props.with`. An error from your source is reported at the include's path. Cycles are rejected, and nesting, including fragments, is limited to `MAX_DEPTH` (64) levels. Fragments are expanded at load time, so a fragment that changes per request means loading per request. Loading costs tens of µs for typical documents (see Performance). Cache the `Ir` per fragment version if that matters.

#### Parameters

`with` passes values into the fragment, so one fragment serves different data:

```yaml
fragments:
  stat:
    type: stack
    children:
      - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ label }}" } }
      - { type: text, props: { value: "{{ value }}" }, style: { color: "{{ tone }}" } }
root:
  type: stack
  children:
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: Revenue, value: "{{ totals.revenue }}", tone: $color.primary } } }
    - { type: include, props: { name: stat, with: { label: In cart, value: "{{ cart.length }}", tone: green } } }
```

A parameter is substituted into the fragment's expressions when the document loads. Inside the fragment above, `{{ value }}` becomes the caller's `{{ totals.revenue }}`, so it behaves exactly as if written in place:
- Server data is filled in on the server.
- An argument that reads state, like `{{ cart.length }}`, keeps updating in the browser.
- An `item` from a list, including one the browser rebuilds, still resolves.

Literal arguments stay literal, so the usual checks apply to them: prop types, `bind` keys, URL policy, and CSS tokens and values. A parameter that is a path or a literal object can be read further (`{{ user.name }}` with `with: { user: "{{ order.customer }}" }`); a computed one (`"{{ a + b }}"`) can't.

Names the fragment uses but no `with` passes are looked up at render time as usual, so fragments can still read the scope they're included in. Defaults are expressions: `{{ size || 'md' }}`. A parameter the fragment never uses gives a warning, which catches typos. A `list` inside the fragment whose `item` or `index` name matches a parameter is an error, since it would hide the parameter.

## Policies

`Engine::new()` trusts the document. `Engine::untrusted()` (or `--untrusted` in the CLI) is for user- or LLM-written configs. It blocks `on*` attributes, `javascript:` URLs, dangerous tags and CSS `expression()`. CSS values that could break out of their declaration are always rejected. So are `data-i-*` attributes, which the runtime reads its bindings and actions from.

lightningcss reports unknown CSS properties and invalid values as **warnings**, because it doesn't know every valid property. Standard properties it doesn't model, such as `border-collapse`, `float` or `pointer-events`, are on an allowlist in `irender-style/src/validate.rs`. Their names are accepted, but their values aren't checked. Use `strict_css` (`--strict-css` in the CLI) to make them errors.

## Performance

```sh
cargo bench -p irender-html                                  # criterion; filter with: -- render/table
cargo bench -p irender-html --features parallel              # adds render/html_parallel/*
cargo run --release -p irender-cli -- render doc.json --data data.json --repeat 200 -o out.html
```

`--timings` / `--repeat N` print parse, resolve, render and serialize times for your own document. Load (parse + resolve) is meant to happen once per document change. Render happens per request.

Results on an Apple M4 Pro, release build (measured 2026-11-24):

| fixture | load | render | per element | render, parallel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| product example (17 elements) | 78 µs | 57 µs | ~3.4 µs | — |
| table, 100 rows (~500 elements) | 32 µs | 438 µs | ~0.88 µs | 206 µs |
| table, 1000 rows (~5000 elements) | 33 µs | 4.28 ms | ~0.86 µs | 1.13 ms |
| 1000 cards with unique styles (~2000 elements) | 5.4 ms | 3.02 ms | ~1.5 µs | — |
| 50 nested levels | 104 µs | 24 µs | ~0.48 µs | — |

**Load** is parse + resolve + CSS validation. **Render, parallel** uses `parallel_min_items = Some(64)`; "—" means the document has no list that large, so it renders on one thread with no overhead.

What keeps rendering fast:
- **Styles are cached by content.** A style block already compiled in this render costs one hash and one comparison (~0.3 µs instead of ~1.4 µs). Built-in components' default styles are built once per process.
- **Browser data is written straight to the output.** Bindings and actions are folded and serialized directly into the HTML, without building intermediate JSON values.
- **Elements borrow from the node.** An element borrows its node's attributes, classes, styles and actions instead of copying them.

`--minify` costs about as much as rendering a small page and saves ~17% of the CSS.

Documents can nest at most ~60 UI levels, and at most 64 counting included fragments. Deeper input is rejected with a located error, which stops hostile input from overflowing the stack.

## Concurrency

**Across requests.** `Engine` and `Ir` are `Send + Sync` (checked at compile time), and `Engine::render` takes `&self` and `&Ir`. Load a document once and render it from any number of threads or async tasks without locks:

```rust
let engine = Arc::new(Engine::new());
let ir = Arc::new(engine.load(src, Format::Json)?);
// in each request handler:
let page = engine.render(&ir, &request_data)?;
```

**Within one page.** With the `parallel` feature, lists with at least `parallel_min_items` items render in chunks on rayon's thread pool:

```rust
let engine = Engine { parallel_min_items: Some(64), ..Engine::new() };  // CLI: --parallel 64
```

The output is byte-identical to a single-thread render, and the first error in document order is reported. This lowers the latency of a large page but uses slightly more total CPU. On a server that is already busy, every core is serving some request, so parallel rendering is off by default. Turn it on when large pages are rare and their latency matters, such as reports, exports or admin tables.

## Features

| crate | feature | default | effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| `irender-core` | `yaml` | yes | Accept `.yaml` / `.yml` documents. |
| `irender-style` | `lightningcss` | yes | Validate CSS declarations and allow `--minify`. |
| `irender-html` | `lightningcss`, `yaml` | yes | Forward to the crates above. |
| `irender-html` | `parallel` | no | Parallel list rendering (`rayon`). The CLI enables it. |

## Tests

```sh
cargo test                                            # everything (the CLI enables `parallel`, so its tests run too)
cargo test -p irender-html                               # renderer without `parallel`
cargo test -p irender-html --features parallel           # renderer with `parallel`
cargo test -p irender-html --test browser -- --ignored   # drives the example in headless Chrome (CHROME=… to override)
```

The browser tests run in WebKit and Firefox too, through a stand-in for Chrome built on Playwright:

```sh
npm ci --prefix tools/playwright && npx --prefix tools/playwright playwright-core install webkit firefox
BROWSER=webkit CHROME=$PWD/tools/playwright/dump-dom.js cargo test --workspace --test browser -- --ignored   # or BROWSER=firefox
```

| suite | covers |
|---|---|
| `irender-core` unit tests + `tests/core.rs` | expressions and type conversions, error paths, JSON vs YAML, prop/style/action/theme validation, untrusted policy, warnings |
| `irender-style` unit tests + `tests/compile.rs` | nesting, selector variants, dynamic values, layer order, dark-mode variables, cache, pinned class names |
| `irender-html/tests/components.rs` | every built-in, `if` markers and `else` chains, list item templates, `include` (scope, sources, cycles, depth, `FragmentDir`), which values update live, actions, URL and `</script>` safety, deterministic output, custom components, rendering from many threads, parallel output identical to sequential |
| `irender-html/tests/runtime_parity.rs` | the browser runtime has its own copy of the expression evaluator; ~90 expressions run through both (Rust, and JS via `node`), and any disagreement fails. Skips with a message if `node` isn't installed. |
| `irender-html/tests/browser.rs` | opt-in, needs Chrome: clicks, types and checks the DOM of the product example; toggles `if` blocks, rebuilds lists from state, runs item-scoped and `mount` actions; binds radios, checkboxes, selects (with options from state) and textareas |

## Custom components

```rust
use irender_html::{Component, Engine, RenderCx, RenderError};
use irender_core::{ComponentInfo, Node, PropDef, PropKind};

struct Badge;
impl Component for Badge {
    fn name(&self) -> &'static str { "badge" }
    fn info(&self) -> ComponentInfo {
        const PROPS: &[PropDef] = &[PropDef::new("text", PropKind::Any, "").required()];
        ComponentInfo { doc: "A badge", props: PROPS, parts: &[], children: false, open_props: false }
    }
    fn render(&self, node: &Node, cx: &mut RenderCx<'_>) -> Result<(), RenderError> {
        let mut el = cx.element("span", node);
        if let Some(text) = node.prop("text") {
            el.text(text);
        }
        cx.open(&el, node)?;
        cx.close("span");
        Ok(())
    }
}

let mut engine = Engine::new();
engine.registry.register(Badge);
```

### Page-level CSS and client behaviours

A component that needs more than per-element styles and the built-in actions can add two kinds of page-level code. Both take `&'static str`, so they come from component code and never from a document:

- `cx.global_css(name, css)` adds a rule such as `@keyframes` once per page, however many instances ask for it.
- `cx.global_js(name, js)` adds a client behaviour's script once per page. `el.behavior(name, config)` marks an element for it. The runtime starts the behaviour on each marked element, including ones an `if` or a rebuilt list inserts later, and calls its `update` after every state change:

```js
(window.__irenderBehaviors ||= {})["counter"] = (el, api) => {
  // api.config (from `behavior`), api.state, api.set(key, value), api.emit(event, detail)
  el.addEventListener("click", () => api.set("n", api.state.n + api.config.step));
  return { update(state) { el.textContent = state.n; } };
};
```

- `cx.early_js(name, js)` adds a script once per page that runs right after the page's `<style>`, before any content is shown. Use it only for what must happen before the first paint. `ui-theme-toggle` uses it to apply a stored colour scheme without a flash.
- `registry.early_js(name, js)` adds such a script to every page rendered with that registry, whatever components it uses. A kit uses it for a setting that covers the whole page: `irender-ui-kit` applies the colour scheme chosen with `ui-theme-toggle` on every page, with a toggle on it or not.

Documents can't mark elements themselves: `data-i-*` attributes are reserved. `irender-ui-kit`'s `ui-combobox` is built this way.

### Passing values to nested components

- `cx.with_context(name, value, f)` makes a `Val` available to the components rendered inside `f`, and `cx.context(name)` reads the innermost one. Documents can't read or set it. A value that depends on an item only the browser knows stays a template, so a dialog can hand its id to the close buttons inside it, even in a list the browser rebuilds.
- `cx.scope_key()` tells the items of a server-rendered list apart, for element ids. Inside a list the browser rebuilds, `cx.client_key()` is a template of the surrounding list indexes (`{{ index }}`) to add as well.

# irender-ui-kit

Ready-made components for [iRender](https://github.com/kaushik-xs/iRender/blob/main/README.md) documents, styled after [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/). Every component is plain config, and nothing needs JavaScript beyond iRender's own runtime. Overlays use the browser's own `<dialog>`, invoker commands, Popover API and CSS anchor positioning.

```rust
let mut engine = irender_html::Engine::new();
irender_ui_kit::register(&mut engine.registry);

let mut doc = irender_core::parse(src, irender_core::Format::Yaml)?;
irender_ui_kit::apply_theme(&mut doc);   // optional: the kit's neutral palette, dark mode included
let ir = engine.resolve(&doc)?;
```

From the CLI, add `--ui-kit` to `validate`, `render` or `components`:

```sh
cargo run -p irender-cli -- render examples/ui-kit/gallery.yaml --ui-kit -o gallery.html
cargo run -p irender-cli -- components --ui-kit      # every component and its props
```

```yaml
- type: ui-card
  props: { title: Create project, description: Deploy your new project in one click. }
  children:
    - { type: ui-input, props: { bind: name, placeholder: Project name } }
    - type: ui-card-footer
      children:
        - { type: ui-button, props: { label: Cancel, variant: outline } }
        - { type: ui-button, props: { label: Deploy } }
```

## Components

**Right to left.** On a page whose `lang` is written right to left (`dir="rtl"`), every component mirrors: what was on the left is on the right, `left` and `right` in `side` and `pin` mean the start and end sides, icons that point along the line turn round, and Left and Right swap in the keyboard (the calendar's next day is to the left) and in dragging. Charts keep their geometry; one-time codes, shortcuts and counts like `2 / 3` read left to right; and a badge takes its direction from its own text.

| component | props | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ui-button` | `label`, `icon`, `variant` (default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link, brand), `size` (default, sm, lg, icon), `href`, `type`, `disabled` | With `href` it renders a link that looks like a button. Children follow the label. A `variant` that reads state follows it. |
| `ui-code-block` | `code` (required), `language`, `title`, `lineNumbers`, `highlight`, `copy` (default true), `wrap`, `maxHeight`, `label` | Code, highlighted for json, yaml, js (ts), rust, python, bash, html, css or sql, with line numbers, marked lines (`[2, "5-7"]`), a copy button that says when it's copied, and a title bar. `code` can read state, and an object shows as JSON; like any prop, a literal with `{{ }}` in it is a template, so code that shows braces comes from state or a list item. The server draws the lines plain, so it reads without the script. Token colours follow `--code-string`, `--code-keyword` and the like. Parts: `head`, `pre`, `copy`; event `copy` with `{ ok }`. |

| `ui-card` | `title`, `description`, `icon`, `variant` (default, elevated, outline, muted), `href`, `tag` | `icon` sits in a tinted square beside the title. `href` makes the whole card a link that lifts when hovered; keep buttons and other links out of it. It's coloured by the theme: the primary colour, a secondary one (`color.brand-2`, else `color.chart-2`, else amber), light tints of both, and neutrals mixed from the text and background colours, so it follows a palette, the custom colours picked with `ui-theme-colors`, and dark mode. `primary` and `secondary` set its own colours (and may use state; null goes back to the theme's). Decorative unless it has a `label`. `animate` (true, or from state) brings it to life a little: a planet floats, a gear turns, a light blinks, sparkles twinkle; still for readers who prefer less motion. The blocks have whole error pages (404, 500, 403, 503, offline, an expired session) and a page of empty states. |

| `ui-tabs` + `ui-tab-panel` | tabs: `bind` (required), `orientation` (horizontal, vertical), `activation` (automatic, manual), `id`; panel: `value`, `label` | `bind` holds the open panel's `value`. Tabs carry `role=tab`, `aria-selected`, `aria-controls`. The list is one stop for Tab; the arrow keys, Home and End move between tabs and select them. More tabs than fit scroll within their list, which keeps the selected one in view and fades on the sides with more. |
| `ui-toggle` | `bind`, `label`, `variant` (default, outline), `size`, `disabled` | `aria-pressed` follows `bind`. |
| `ui-toggle-group` | `bind`, `options`, `multiple`, `variant`, `size`, `disabled` | One option pressed at most; pressing it again sets `bind` to null. With `multiple`, `bind` holds a list and each press adds or removes its option. Wraps when it's wider than what it's in. |
| `ui-theme-toggle` | `labels` (`{ system, light, dark }`), `variant` (default `outline`), `size` (default `sm`) | System / Light / Dark. Light and Dark override `prefers-color-scheme` for the theme's dark mode and `@dark` styles; the choice is kept in `localStorage` (`irender-theme`) and applied before the page is shown, so a reload doesn't flash. Every page rendered with the kit applies it, with a toggle on it or not. Its behaviour is added only to pages that use it. |
| `ui-theme-option` | `option` (required), `swatch` (a token, or a list for several dots), `label`, `variant` (default `outline`), `size` (default `sm`) | Picks a choice of a theme option for every page; see [Theme options](#theme-options). |
| `ui-theme-panel` | `options` (default: every theme option), `mode` (default true) | A labelled `ui-theme-option` per option, palette first and chart colours last, and the mode. Put it in a `ui-popover` for a Theme button. |
| `ui-theme-colors` | `option` (default `palette`), `gradients` (default true), `backgrounds` (default true) | Colour inputs (picked, or typed as hex) for a custom primary and second brand colour, each with an optional gradient end, and the backgrounds of the page, cards, popovers, dialogs, sheets and the sidebar; changing one picks the `custom` choice. `ui-theme-panel` shows it under the palette. |
| `ui-dialog` | `trigger`, `triggerVariant`, `title`, `description`, `id` | A modal `<dialog>`. Escape, its ✕ or a click outside closes it. |
